feedback_comments: Friendly service & neat building. Depending on the atmosphere you are looking for, the music is a bit loud.

They have a super friendly staff and a simple modern decor. I enjoyed the Six Degrees of Kevin Bacon exhibit on display. I got a really young and hip vibe from this place, and the sandwiches are amazing!

We've heard that we need to go to places in Ybor and try them out, so we set out to find a place for dinner.  One thing is for sure...the menu has traditional food, but in a unique way.  

I ordered the deluxe grilled cheese (has tomatoes, pesto, whole wheat) and my husband had the BBQ pig quesadilla.  Both dishes were good, but I don't feel like they were 'awesome'.  

We went out on a limb and tried the hibiscus sangria and the chocolate espresso cake for dessert.  The cake was VERY espresso!  Too rich for me!  The sangria definitely tasted like flowers, but in a good way. It was pretty refreshing too!

 It was fun to try a new place, but I don't think we'll go back.

This place is listed as vegetarian-friendly and it is, provided that you eat eggs, cheese, and whatever else they put on the food without listing it in the menu description. Unfortunately this place was a nightmare for me as a vegan. I ordered the veggie cuban with no swiss or honey mustard since those were the only non-vegan ingredients listed in the description, and if it wasn't for the server mentioning "oh that's a great choice; the chef puts an egg on it too," then I would have gotten a sandwich with egg. After I stressed "no animal products, no egg, no dairy, no butter," the server responded with "oh well you know the egg isn't actually meat" as opposed to, you know, respecting my dietary restrictions.

I have no intention of returning, due to the lack of clarity on the menu and the server's rudeness when I was expressing my allergies/restrictions. Maybe if the restaurant lists all of the ingredients and trains their staff on how to not be rude to someone who was rightfully annoyed at almost getting an item I couldn't eat, then it might be worth a recommendation. But then again, it's not a vegan-friendly establishment despite it being vegetarian-friendly.
It sucks, don't go!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Cold food, stuck up waiters, expensive drinks
Great bar/café! Such a great place to hang, inside is beautiful and outside you can hear nice music while having a coffee and a cig! Definitely coming back! Loved it

We walked into The Bricks of Ybor and were immediately greeted by the owner and taken on a tour. He showed us the studio area next door, the small patio in the back, and the food prep area. He also explained the menu and gave some recommendations. I've never been treated that way at a restraunt and it was an awesome touch. The food was great. The waitress did bring my husband the wrong sandwich but by the time we figured it out, it wasn't worth mentioning. He liked whatever it was she brought him. The beer selection was very good. The atmosphere is laid back and unique. They have games to play while you enjoy your drinks. The music is awesome. All in all, I love this place!

Either ate or had drinks here a few times over the summer as my office was just upstairs.  I'm not a vegetarian, but the Goodness wrap is a knockout.  I also greatly enjoyed the chili I had here, though it was a special so I'm not sure how often it comes around.  I'm not really into the hipster vibe of the staff, but I never had any service problems and that's what is most important.  

I definitely don't live or die by The Bricks but it's a place I would suggest if you're ever in Ybor City.

Just came here for cocktails on a Tuesday night. The bar was full but not very busy otherwise. We got the huckle punch and Constantine. The huckleberry vodka in the huckle punch is one of my favorites so loved that drink and the Constantine also very good if you like bourbon! Service was very good and prices were reasonable. Had $3 taco deals and a very cute coffee bar so would definetly be interested in coming back to eat or for a good studying place!
Easily my favorite overall spot in Ybor. The food is freaking amazing, the staff is awesome and know their booze/beer, and it just has a great feel.

I'm defintely a fan. The food/drinks are always stellar and while the staff is super friendly, the only issue with The Bricks is the time it takes to order/be served. It isn't like the servers are slow either, they are clearly working their assess off running from table to table, so maybe it is that people have called in sick the couple of times I've been in recently and they had to work twice as hard but a Sunday lunch shouldn't take 3 hours. Now that my complaining is out of the way, the restaurant itself is super groovy. The kitchen is on full display so no crazy stories of chefs putting anything crazy into your food here. And they look like they are having a great time while they prepare meals (whether they are or not, I love to see people enjoy what they do). I normally get draft beer but their cocktails look really interesting and innovative. At lunch, I normally get the "Goodness" which is a hummus wrap and it comes with a choice of a side ($8). Don't bother being wishy-washy on the side, get the Asian slaw, it is delicious, and if available I would order as a meal. The wrap was good but the star was the slaw. Thai, pea-nutty, goodness:) I've gotten the Elvis before ($8) and it was delicious but something I can make a home. I ordered it without bacon. My husband ordered the burrito and loved it as well ($9). Others at our table raved about the Chicken and the Pig, The BBQ pork, and The Cure sandwiches. Everyone really liked their food. The Bricks really is a great spot on the 7th Avenue strip, perfect for late night people watching that make Ybor awesome and also out of the way enough to not feel like it's distinctly part of the Ybor scene.

For days I have tried to put a side the terrible experince I had, I really don't like to put a bad review, but most of all I deeply appreciate when businesses treat everyone with respect and priority, and for some reason and actually for no reason. I walked in and noticed I have to go to the bar for srvice, there were no available seats, so I stood at the beginning of the bar from the entrance, made an eye contact with the bar tender, 5 min passed he still didn't come to me so I looked over for a menu and grabbed it myself, shortly after he reached to me and took my order of drinks and food... 10 min passed and he didn't prepare my drinks, he left the bar area, and another guy came to replace him, he asked us if we needed help, I told him we already ordered, mean while I'm waiting and waiting and I see our server went to take out food for people, totally forgot about us, he could have at least tell the other two guys who were at the bar ( one of them was the owner) to make us the drink... Then the owner came to me and he told me I should have told the guy that replaced him to make me the drinks, i told him how could I know it works that way? And instead of trying to make excuses for why I don't have my drinks and blaming me for it, he obviously didn't care for what u had to say but I tried explain him how long I've been waiting and that I should have been taken care off and that he's been very rude for trying to excuse the situation instead of handling It property... End of story, He got mad he said I'm the owner and that I'm not going to talk to him that way and he walked away from me! So to sum it all up, I waited a while until I was served, the tender argued with me that chocolate always has milk inside ( just a lack of knowledge) the owner saw us waiting and waiting , looked at us while serving others, and than he got the nerve to be mad at me for being upset....!!!!
My favorite lunch spot in Ybor. Best greek salad of all time. Great servise.
Excellent service, trendy yet comfortable atmosphere, and very nice food. About half the items we requested weren't available b/c they're transitioning to a new menu.

My friend and I visited Tampa for a concert, and about ten minutes away from the Atlanta airport he realized that he had purchased tickets for the wrong day. We had already made hotel reservations and bought the concert tickets, so he just had to pay same-day price for airfare: all in all about $800 more. "It was totally worth it," he later told me, "Because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life."

All because we randomly picked the Bricks of Ybor from Yelp. I can't vouch for the peanut butter or meatless menu, but the meat sandwiches that we bought were absolutely phenomenal. I had the pulled pork, which was flavored with ponzu and served on Hawaiian sweet bread. It was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. We spent a few hours hanging out and drinking, during which time Brian, the owner, came out and talked to us, comped us a drink, let us try new appetizers he was developing (all for free) and generally made us feel really welcome. 

I kept my eyes open to the kind of crowd that came in and out of the restaurant. It seemed to draw everything from hipsters to geriatrics and strait-laced families with young kids. I think it speaks to both the diversity of the menu and the pleasant environment. We went back for drinks before and after the concert. It got very crowded but we still received excellent food, drinks and service. I give this restaurant my strongest recommendation, and it's the first place I'm going when I next visit Tampa.

The Bricks is a tasty restaurant for lunch with a cool and unique Ybor City atmosphere along with friendly service! The only reason it didn't get 5 stars is because it is a little pricey for the quantities.

I dig the art and the choices on the menu.

Skanky Chai is pretty good. 

The Elvis was pretty awesome. Peanut butter, bacon, and bananas on cuban toast. 
That sounds a lot like something I would drool over.

Nice!

I went there for dinner while in the Tampa area and had a great meal.   They have multiple Vegan and Vegetarian options, while also having a full bar with Guinness.   Very unusual across the good ole USA.

The place is in an interesting area, which seems it could be a little rough in the dark, so if you go, I would recommend going during the light hours.

The bartenders are really nice, and helpful with picking a good dish.
Just went there yesterday for brunch...  I've had a ton of grilled cheese sandwiches but this makes my top five. Loved the atmosphere. So happy we gave this restaurant a chance.

I ordered the Kung fury bowl and it's pretty good, just not a huge fan of Asian slaw. The restaurant is pretty cool with the decoration and not at a super crowded location in ybor. The service was a bit slow, but the food came pretty quick.

Great environment, good assortments of beers, funky people, board games, chill vibes, Monday Game nights and random parties, outside patio, great coffee, try liquid heroin coffee, one of my favorite places in town
Came for Father's day brunch, and will definitely come back. great selection of vegetarian food.  Veggie Cuban and cheese grits were awesome. .and service was so good!

I read the reviews on Yelp and decided to check out Bricks of Ybor for myself. 

Nice atmosphere and hip music playing in the background. I sat at the bar and watched the flat screen televisions (they were playing the History Channel on one TV. & "Shaun of the Dead" on another TV.). 

Good beer on tap (I tried the IPA -- it was good) and a small menu specializing in appetizers, salads & sandwiches. I ordered the hummus plate and the iceberg wedge salad -- both were delicious. The blue cheese dressing on the salad was particularly scrumptious. 

For one beer and an app and a salad, my bill came to just under $25 before tip -- kinda expensive (considering they no longer serve the "salmon spread" on the hummus plate -- should that really be priced at $10, still?).

Tasty place to grab a unique sandwich or something else with some tasty beer. I love the decor in this restaurant, as it seems to marry bricks, random tomfoolery, and nerdiness quite well. I've enjoyed most things there. The Bird and Pig was quite good as well as their veggie burger. They also have lots of theme nights, but I've never been to one.

The Bricks gets a "1" in my book because they have terrible servise. Great food, but terrible service. I went there about 3pm on a Tuesday...which happened to be my birthday to have lunch with my mother. Not only were we not greeted by the 3 staff standing around with NO other customers, but we were also not brought any menus or given direction about seating. We sat down and waited for a server to come by and ask for our drink order and bring menus. No one ever did. We got up and grabbed our own menus close to where the staff were standing. They paid no attention. After 3 or 4 more minutes we stood up to leave and they didn't care. So we walked out and I had my birthday lunch elsewhere. I wrote to them on Facebook about our service and they promptly deleted my comment and ignored my message. I used to go to the Bricks all the time, but we've never been back since and I warn any new friends to not go there as well.

nice place for gatherings and hanging out. Friendly staff. 

Food was OK. Not bad, not good, it just sat somewhere in the middle.

One of my favorite spots to swing by while in the Ybor area, either with a group of friends or alone, as they do have a lot of space to bring out your laptop to work or read. Since I usually come during the workday for lunch, I'm a big fan of their specialty coffee drinks. They have a very unique one - espresso lemonade - which I got to try on my last visit. The bitterness was cancelled out by the lemonade and it was delicious. The Bricks has a good choice of apps/salads/sandwiches and I also tried a spicy chorizo, creamed soup, which my server recommended, and he was right-on point with this pick. If you're in Ybor please make sure you stop by here...it's vegan/vegetarian friendly and just has a good all-around vibe inside.

The Bricks has a super cool vibe. I've visited multiple times for dinner and once for drinks. I'm always impressed with their sandwiches and other food. Normally everything is very fresh and tasty. They have a good sized line up of craft beers most of them local to the area, which is something I'm always looking for. 

It's sort of a dive-y location on the outskirts of the main part of Ybor. Late night they have a small menu of appetizers/small plates and have a DJ. It's clientele leads to some awesome people watching. 

All in all, definitely worth a try. It's not super fancy, so it's perfect for a casual dinner or a new place to try to grab a beer (there's a full bar as well).
fun place with a nice atmosphere. Ordered the Elvis which is a good sandwich with peanut butter honey bananana and bacon! it sounds weird but it was delicious.
My favorite drinks place to imbibe before a show in Ybor. Kyle is spot on every time with what is seemingly the exact thing I want before I even know it. Also, the nachos. Trust me!

Visited The Bricks this evening for dinner with a group of 6 and I think I can say we all enjoyed our experience  - I give it a solid 3-stars because I wasn't blown away by the food, ambiance or service but all were good if not a little above average. 

I started with an Old Fashioned which was sadly, quite watered down.  The table started with the Bricklayer Nachos which were good and a pretty decent size portion too.  For my dinner I had the Mediterranean Grilled Cheese - feta and mozzarella cheese, olive tapenade, baby spinach and portabello mushroom pressed in a piece of flatbread.  The first few bites were enjoyable but about a quarter of the way into it I realized how SALTY it was.  Unfortunately, it was a little one-note and better in concept than in execution in my opinion. 

Our waitress was pleasant and split the check 6-ways without us even having to ask, which I thought was really nice of her.  Atmosphere was unique but nothing worth coming back for.

Also, worth noting - The Bricks doesn't have its own parking lot so you'll have to find street parking (good luck), a paid parking lot lot or one of the local parking garages.
I love this place. Everything I've had seems really fresh. The hummus is really tasty and the ambiance is nice and relaxed.

2 words THE CURE! I ended up here after a night of one too many drinks (it happens). A friend recommended this place for a hang over cure! She was not mistaken! After reviewing their menu, which seemed a bit obnoxious, (I'm talking quirky names that require you read the description to be able to decipher what you're eating) I settled on the sandwich with an egg on it! Im a sucker for a runny egg on just about anything! Messy eggs, bacon, mozzarella, jalapeño aioli, on toasted cuban bread; this holy grail of a sandwich is called THE CURE! I have been back a few times to this establishment just for this sandwich, the mimosas too. Oh yea they have liquor so you can totally have drinks here. The ambience is very chill. There are a good amount of tables inside and bar seating; no outside seating. I have been here on a Sunday for brunch and found it to be pretty family/kid friendly. The whole place and most of the staff is painfully hipster but it works. The bathrooms are clean and there is a small back patio with mural art.
Friendly service & neat building. Depending on the atmosphere you are looking for, the music is a bit loud.

It is definitely a place to bring your friends and chat. I love their different types of Peanut Butter sandwiches. Amazing! Not only that, but the inside environment is just so positive and provides inspiration.

This is THE BEST spot for food and drinks in Ybor. The drinks are amazing and the food is top notch. Cool, laid back atmosphere and amazing bar!! All of the staff are helpful and accommodating!! Best happy hour!!!

We cam here for my wife's birthday this year that also just so happens to be Cinco De Mayo. We didn't want to go to a mexican joint so we chose the Bricks after reading some specials that they had going online. I have to say it was a good night and a lot of fun. Good drinks as well as food. Great ambiance, this is an older building in Ybor that they really did a great job of restoring. These guys are always having great food and happy hour specials. You won't be disappointed.

Where do i start with this place! I love that they have local art on the walls/ always doing art shows the staff that works there always rocking smiles talking to all the guess a all around good atmosphere vibe I tip my hat to the head chef (Chef Ben) The food is always on point and i like when the cooks yell "ORDER UP" hahaha I can wright a book about how awesome this place is KEEP UP THE GOOD WORK and SEE YOU SOON!

I thoroughly enjoy going to the Bricks.  It's unique atmosphere with cheap, but tasty, food options combine for a great experience.  

The term hipster is thrown around a lot these days and while you may be greeted and surrounded by people in skinny jeans, wearing Toms shoes, IMAX glasses, and an extra piercing, you are treated no differently.  I always feel warmly welcomed and entertained.  

As it does have a large bar, it may get rowdy in the evenings, but the Bricks maintains a family-friendly atmosphere.  

I ate the Bird and Pig meal once, very very good, and the breakfast bagel the next time.  The fiancee had black bean soup and a grilled cheese sandwich.  Very tasty combination. 

Highly recommend!

Great atmosphere, always a good variety of music playing, excellent food and an increasingly diverse drink menu make this possibly my favorite place in Tampa. The Bird and Pig could quite possibly be the best sandwich in the history of sandwiches! Chicken, bacon, Brie, agave on Hawaiian sweet bread....yum! Also, try Root Down on the drink menu. Tastes exactly like Root Beer!
Came for Father's day brunch, and will definitely come back. great selection of vegetarian food.  Veggie Cuban and cheese grits were awesome. .and service was so good!

First of all I would like to say this is a pretty cool place. They have a great selection of beer and booze. The bartenders were very attentive and made awesome drinks. I was there on a Thursday night with a wedding party of about 12 people and we were having a great night. This is where I would love to end this review because based on the atmosphere and bartenders, this is a really chill place to hang out in ybor. Unfortunately, there is more to the story.

Later in the night, the bar started clearing out. The only people in the bar were myself, the wedding party I was with, the bartenders, and 3 other people. That's it. We (the wedding party) thought it would be fun to do the wobble and since the DJ was playing hip-hip anyway, we figured that it wouldn't be an issue to request that he play the wobble. After All, there wasn't many people in the bar anyway. Upon requesting to the DJ that we would like him to play the wobble he proceeded to respond with statements like "I refuse to play that song" "I don't like that song" "I'm not a jukebox". After briefly sharing our differences of opinion, I went to the bar to get a drink. At this time the DJ also walked up to the bar as we were kindly telling the bartender that they might want to reconsider their DJ choices because he was more concerned with what he wanted to hear, rather than what the patrons of the bar wanted to hear. Upon sharing our opinion with the bartender, the DJ butts in again to express that "I'm the DJ, and I'll play what I want to hear" that irritated me and I got a little heated. The bartender proceeded to cut me off because I argued with the DJ. I totally understand that, the bartender did the right thing there to calm down a situation. 

Point of my long story is, I really hope this place reconsiders their DJ choices in the future. They need someone that will play what the patrons want to hear and not what he wants to hear. Maybe that's just my opinion, but I feel that I make a strong case considering that by the time it was all said and done, our party was the only people in the bar. So, instead of 5 stars, I'm marking it a 3 based on the DJ alone.

This might be my first five star rating. This place was absolutely awesome and I cannot wait until I go back for a second time. Our sever, Millie, was friendly and efficient from the moment we sat down. The atmosphere of the place was unique, and the food was among the most unique in Tampa that I have experienced in years. I got the pork tacos for an appetizer and the "bird and pig" for lunch. The sandwich was so good I could have ordered it again. Overall it was a fantastic experience and I will be returning for their drink specials.

The Bricks is a hipster haven, but don't let that deter you if you don't wear non-prescription glasses and flannel. I'm always the least cool person in here and no one seems to mind. (Although maybe I AM cool -- last time I was here the DJ was playing Hall & Oates most likely to be ironic, but I genuinely enjoyed it.) The menu is mostly sandwiches and some salads. It's all about the Bird & Pig sandwich. I have a hard time straying from this delicacy of chicken, bacon, brie, and apples on pressed sweet bread. Sweet, check. Salty, check. Crunchy, check. Nice selection of local and craft brews, too.

I dined here for the first time with my daughter, who is a regular. We had the Hummus appetizer. I had the Bricks Club and she had the specialty Grilled Cheese. The food was fresh, tasty and full of flavor. The service was very good. The bottle of ice water they bring is a classy touch. The ambiance is eclectic. My daughter told me normally the place is full of hipsters, but the crowd was spare on the day we were there. The prices are reasonable and in line with the usual and customary norms for Tampa. I don't drink, but it looked like they have quite an assortment of craft beer available.

Recently stopped in during a bar crawl for some drinks and Battletoads. Couldn't eat the buzz away, but loved what I saw. Photos on walls showed the transformation from Tahiti Joe's/Latitudes into The Bricks of today, and brought back some old Ybor memories. The staff was kind, and the video game corner was a blast. Delicious coffee, and had an artsy feel as well. Every food item that passed our sniffers en route to their respective hipster pie holes was cause for comment. I will certainly be coming by for a sammich at this place.

It was so difficult deciding what to order here. I was in the mood for a skanky chai latte, but the skinny bitch latte just had that calorie conscious ring to it. After a bit of thought I decided, skanky it shall be! This has got to be one of my favorite places in Tampa. I had never really put a pulse on "hipster" in Tampa, but I found the closest thing to it at Bricks. Plenty of space to lounge here with a nice offering that ranged from caffeinated beverages to brews and snacks. I would have never typically thought to throw bacon on a peanut butter and banana sandwich and then drizzle with honey, but I'm glad someone did. The Elvis sandwich is a hunka, hunka, burning yum! I would give this place five stars all day, except for the fact that service is slow. Like, dial-up slow. Like larvae to butterfly metamorphosis slow. So slow in fact that on a pretty *slow* afternoon, it would take 20 minutes just to get an iced chai even though you have a clear view of queue and activity of the servers. So slow that from time of check request to actually receiving it, was about another 20 minutes. While the laid back atmosphere is one of the things that makes this place so cool, it's also the incredibly laid back service that could put a damper on things if you're in a rush.

Cheaper than the $$ rating by far, depending on your interests (I had the $5.50 grilled peanut butter and Gouda). And I didn't think the combination would work, but I was wrong. It's not my absolute favorite peanut butter sandwich, but it's tasty. Sadly, the "peanut butter bars" don't have as extensive a list of ingredients as they did when Brett N. visited. I also tasted a forkful of Jodi's Greek salad (which was all that was left!), and that lemon-dill vinaigrette just made my "next time we're here" list.

It is definitely a place to bring your friends and chat. I love their different types of Peanut Butter sandwiches. Amazing! Not only that, but the inside environment is just so positive and provides inspiration.

If you're immune to salmonella poisoning then this is the perfect place for you! Very overpriced, minimum effort in providing authentic food NOT out of a can. They undercook the chicken and it taste like refrigerator. Please don't waste your hard earned cash on half assed food. Unless you just want drinks and a good time with friends, don't come here.

The Bricks gets a "1" in my book because they have terrible service.  Great food, but terrible service. 

I went there about 3pm on a Tuesday...which happened to be my birthday to have lunch with my mother.  Not only were we not greeted by the 3 staff standing around with NO other customers, but we were also not brought any menus or given direction about seating.

They paid no attention.  After 3 or 4 more minutes we stood up to leave and they didn't care. So we walked out and I had my birthday lunch elsewhere. 

I  wrote to them on Facebook about our service and they promptly deleted my comment and ignored my message.  

I used to go to the Bricks all the time, but we've never been back since and I warn any new friends to not go there as well.

I've always thought the idea of apple on a sandwich (that didn't involve peanut butter) as completely preposterous, because sweet things do not belong on sandwiches!  

So what did I order at The Bricks?  Naturally, the Bird and Pig - which features chicken, bacon, apple, brie and agave nectar.   It was definitely sweet.  And savory.  And absolutely, positively to die for.  I loved every scrumptious bite of it.... except for the dry chicken breast.  I'm not sure if it was just old, but either way it was dry and disappointing.

Next on the menu was the deluxe grilled cheese sandwich, which was all sorts of yummy cheese, smothering delicious garden fresh basil (wow!), spinach and tomato.   The first bite of this sandwich was knock-your-socks-off.  The basil really stands out and it definitely warranted an audible moan.  The next few bites weren't as spectacular, but I still loved the sandwich.  I'd go with the Bird and Pig again if I had to choose.

While we waited, we treated our faces to black bean dip (suggested by the waiter) and we enjoyed it.  If you like black bean dip, then you'll like this one.  

We washed all of that down with a glass of liquid heroin, and all was right with the world.

The end.

Oh, and the service - spot on.  The place is cute, the staff is attentive, and it's clear this place easily doubles as a comfy daytime spot and a lovely night spot - if that's your kinda thing.
Really like the Bricks. Always a new experience when i go. The coffee, good. The cocktails, better! The ambiance is hip. The food is pretty good too.
Great atmosphere and service, food and drinks were excellent. Everything was fresh.  Bird and the pig sandwich was delicious, also the pacific rim. Will return soon.
Great craft beers, friendly bartenders, and AMAZING, delicious food. The vegetarian Cuban sandwich was wonderful!

Food is terrible. Nacho dip was covered in there advacado cream dressing which was bad. Very sloppy. The pesto grilled cheese, was covered in way too much pesto. Again very sloppy. Overall bad food, chef must be high or something. Oh and found a few ants crawling up my leg. Will never come back.

We waited an hour for our food. No coffee refills the entire time. We saw our food souring in the window for 20 minutes. When we finally left the server said it couldn't be helped. No apologies, no service, no food, no tip.

We went at a slow time on a weekday afternoon for a late lunch because we were all wanting sandwiches. So between us all we had: the Bird & Pig, BBQ quesadilla, ahi BLT, clubhouse and kids pbj. All the sandwiches were great! Service was a bit slow though. If I was in the area again I may try again but I would not go out of my way to eat here.
Great atmosphere and service, food and drinks were excellent. Everything was fresh.  Bird and the pig sandwich was delicious, also the pacific rim. Will return soon.
Excellent service, trendy yet comfortable atmosphere, and very nice food. About half the items we requested weren't available b/c they're transitioning to a new menu.
Great craft beers, friendly bartenders, and AMAZING, delicious food. The vegetarian Cuban sandwich was wonderful!

staff is awesome and food is damn good. drinks are a reasonable price and Andrew always has something awesome/weird playing on the TV. If the independent were cooler, it would be the Bricks. One of the gods invented the bird and pig. Definitely get that.The cure is pretty tasty too, I'd eat it again. The place has cool wall art, a comfortable back patio, and Paper Mario characters on the bathroom doors. Have to appreciate the subtle nerdiness.

Based this visit entirely upon previous Yelp reviews, which as usual we're spot on. Great atmosphere and feel to this place - Kind of an art house meets coffee house meets Animal House environment. Very unusual. In a good way. The servise was relaxed, social and great. The beverages were delicous and the menu was quite interesting. I so wanted the food to be much better than it was. Tried the Bird and Pig, a specialty grilled cheese and a couple apps. Everything was good but not great. In truth, if I was judging on food alone, there would be three stars instead of four. But the atmosphere and the staff clearly deserved the extra star, and I'll head back to try some other items on the menu next visit.

The Bricks completely lives up to the hype. Don't leave without trying their amazing Basil-infused lemonade!

Really chill cafe-like vibe, with a creative comfort food menu (peanut butter sandwiches!), and full table service.

In a few weeks they will be opening a quiet "study hall" space for laptop lurkers, making this a killer telecommute/study spot.

Recently stopped in during a bar crawl for some drinks and Battletoads. Couldn't eat the buzz away, but loved what I saw. Photos on walls showed the transformation from Tahiti Joe's/Latitudes into The Bricks of today, and brought back some old Ybor memories. The staff was kind, and the video game corner was a blast. Delicious coffee, and had an artsy feel as well. Every food item that passed our sniffers en route to their respective hipster pie holes was cause for comment. I will certainly be coming by for a sammich at this place.

A must when you are in Ybor.  I ate and drank here multiple times a day for my 5 day trip to Tampa.  Every single meal was spectacular.  The Skinny bitch latte is perfect to start the day.  The proper grilled cheese is amazing, just wish they would have tomato soup to go along with it.  And you can't find better bartenders anywhere else in town.

The Bricks gets a "1" in my book because they have terrible service.  Great food, but terrible service. 

I went there about 3pm on a Tuesday...which happened to be my birthday to have lunch with my mother.  Not only were we not greeted by the 3 staff standing around with NO other customers, but we were also not brought any menus or given direction about seating.  

We sat down and waited for a server to come by and ask for our drink order and bring menus.  No one ever did.  We got up and grabbed our own menus close to where the staff were standing.  They paid no attention.  After 3 or 4 more minutes we stood up to leave and they didn't care. So we walked out and I had my birthday lunch elsewhere. 

I  wrote to them on Facebook about our service and they promptly deleted my comment and ignored my message.  

I used to go to the Bricks all the time, but we've never been back since and I warn any new friends to not go there as well.

Lots of vegetarian options. The servise was pretty fast. The skateboard wall was nice (Calvin & Hobbes represent!). The sandwich I got was a bit lacking in the flavor department. Really didn't know what to eat since I went here at night just before a binge of dancing and drinking. Didn't really feel into the peanut butter at that point in time. Next time I'll try their peanut butter creations, but I'll probably go for brunch or a late lunch since it seems the menu is more designed for that and not any pre-gaming.

Where do I start: Phenomenal food Excellent Bartender - I didn't know what to drink and bartender created one to her liking Great Atmosphere Great music - DJ on Friday Night was awesome Even the free water in the beginning tasted amazingly Definitely would go again

The Bricks completely lives up to the hype. Don't leave without trying their amazing Basil-infused lemonade!

Really chill cafe-like vibe, with a creative comfort food menu (peanut butter sandwiches!), and full table service.

In a few weeks they will be opening a quiet "study hall" space for laptop lurkers, making this a killer telecommute/study spot.

One of my favorite spots to swing by while in the Ybor area, either with a group of friends or alone, as they do have a lot of space to bring out your laptop to work or read. Since I usually come during the workday for lunch, I'm a big fan of their specialty coffee drinks. They have a very unique one - espresso lemonade - which I got to try on my last visit. The bitterness was cancelled out by the lemonade and it was delicious. The Bricks has a good choice of apps/salads/sandwiches and I also tried a spicy chorizo, creamed soup, which my server recommended, and he was right-on point with this pick. If you're in Ybor please make sure you stop by here...it's vegan/vegetarian friendly and just has a good all-around vibe inside.

The husband and I had a kid free day so we decided to have a (gasp) lunch date. We picked The Bricks because...well why the hell not. As soon as we walked in I loved the place. It was bright and cozy at the same time. The staff was super friendly and we got the vibe that we could hang out all day if we wanted. I ordered the most delicous "adult" coffee to drop kick the sleepiness out of my head. The coffee was SUPER yummy and the liquor did the trick. It took me a while to figure out what I wanted to eat because everything on the menu looked soooo good and I was super hungry. In the end, I decided on the Harvest Grill Cheese Sandwich.....nom nom noom.....I was not dissappointed. It hit the spot and filled my belly with melty cheesy goodness. The bread was fresh, crunchy, tender and tasty. The sandwich innards were porportioned perfect. The Gouda, bacon and apple playing off each other in perfect harmony. GO HERE AND EAT! I cannot wait to go again and feel this will be a staple on our lunch resturant list. Even if your not hungry this would be a wonderful place to have a drink and just chill day or night. Thanks Bricks for a great lunch!

Came hungry and left full but not stuffed. The goodness wrap was named appropriately. Hummus with cucumber, tomato, lettuce, feta cheese and I added avocado was very flavorful. No need for any sauce of any kind. Had the potato salad as a side and though it was a bit bland, added a little salt to it, it was still good. Glad they don't add mayo to it and tasted home made for sure. Nice ambience too, decorated for Halloween. I'm not a fan of TV's while dining, but will always give a pass when they have good tunes playing so don't have to listen to TV. Only saw 2 servers on but it wasn't that busy on this Sunday afternoon. Server was knowledgeable and personable so not sure why others complained about rudeness. Saw none of that.

Seems like a good place ...very chill and low key..not my particular favorite food ( more on the healthy side) but still good quality food and service with a fun video game theme once a week ...good place to check out
nice place for gatherings and hanging out. Friendly staff. Food was OK. Not bad, not good, it just sat somewhere in the middle.

We went at a slow time on a weekday afternoon for a late lunch because we were all wanting sandwiches. So between us all we had: the Bird & Pig, BBQ quesadilla, ahi BLT, clubhouse and kids pbj. All the sandwiches were great! Service was a bit slow though. If I was in the area again I may try again but I would not go out of my way to eat here.

Either ate or had drinks here a few times over the summer as my office was just upstairs. I'm not a vegetarian, but the Goodness wrap is a knockout. I also greatly enjoyed the chili I had here, though it was a special so I'm not sure how often it comes around. I'm not really into the hipster vibe of the staff, but I never had any service problems and that's what is most important. I definitely don't live or die by The Bricks but it's a place I would suggest if you're ever in Ybor City.

While I was in Tampa for the last 2 years, The Bricks was a second home. Great food and even greater people. I moved back to Seattle and left making friends. Wish I could've brought The Bricks and my new friends back with me. Definitely a place for locals and visitors to check out!

Tasty place to grab a unique sandwich or something else with some tasty beer. I love the decor in this restaurant, as it seems to marry bricks, random tomfoolery, and nerdiness quite well. I've enjoyed most things there. The Bird and Pig was quite good as well as their veggie burger. They also have lots of theme nights, but I've never been to one.

nice place for gatherings and hanging out. Friendly staff. 

Food was OK. Not bad, not good, it just sat somewhere in the middle.

Cheaper than the $$ rating by far, depending on your interests (I had the $5.50 grilled peanut butter and Gouda). And I didn't think the combination would work, but I was wrong. It's not my absolute favorite peanut butter sandwich, but it's tasty. Sadly, the "peanut butter bars" don't have as extensive a list of ingredients as they did when Brett N. visited.

I also tasted a forkful of Jodi's Greek salad (which was all that was left!), and that lemon-dill vinaigrette just made my "next time we're here" list.

Wanted to try the pig and bird sammich but when I got there I decided on the Pacific Rim. The Asian slaw and bbq theme was too much to pass up. I thought the sandwich was really good and had a nice balance to it. I got chips and queso as my side but with this sandwich fries would have been the go to. They don't have fries so you'll have to choose something else. 

Service at the bar was really good, there were multiple people that helped me during my meal. One thing is they were out of three of the beers I wanted right off the bat. 

Pretty cool vibe in the place and people just hanging with friends having drinks and food.

I had high expectations when I went to this place recently after some recommendations from friends.  We visited on a night when there weren't very crowded so it was nice to be able to have such an attentive waitress and service.  I was a bit disappointed when I didn't find as much on the menu as I would have liked to have seen that would appeal to me.  I guess I have become very picky with my Yelp addiction in terms of scrutinizing every establishment I go to pretty thoroughly.  

I ordered the hummus appetizer for the table and was very pleased at the quality of the dish.  For my entree I ordered their Bricks Salad which had plenty of fresh produce packed in.  I ordered a double portion of chicken for it, which still seemed pretty skimpy especially since I was charged for that request.  Overall, I'd say this is probably one of Ybor's lesser known spots as its more on the western edge of the main strip, yet it seems very lively and upbeat.  I did like that they had featured lots of artwork by various local artists that were on display and offerred for sale.  Not a bad place to hang out and have a drink if you're looking for a lower key outing in the Ybor area.

They have a super friendly staff and a simple modern decor.

I enjoyed the Six Degrees of Kevin Bacon exhibit on display.

I got a really young and hip vibe from this place, and the sandwiches are amazing!

Full disclosure: My experience might just have been an isolated, rare occurrence. I arrived to The Brick and sat myself at the bar. After 15 minutes of zero service I was getting ready to leave but I noticed the waiting staff on the main floor looked active and on top of things. I decided to transition from the lack of service bar to the main floor and, literally, as soon as I sat down I had a waiter hand me a menu, take my drink order and before even a blink I had a Bloody Mary in front on me. Moral of this story, careful sitting at the bar since the service there seemed to be lacking. I'm sure it was the timing since my overall experience was a thumbs up. 

I ordered the loaded Bloody Mary. The drink was simple but very delightful, clearly proving that less is more. The drink had a little satisfying kick that's normal to any Bloody Mary. Overall- very satisfied with their Bloody Mary, so much in fact I ordered two. Maybe a little more body to it but not a must. 

Food: I ordered the Tuna BLT with the side of Asian slaw. Overall: GREAT. The theme here is clearly simple. They exploit every taste which is gratifying since that's the most important thing. The slaw was crisp and surprisingly very refreshing. Now, the tuna can only be described as crafted by a masterful craftsman! Yes, I said it. It tasted better than it looked and that's hard todo since it looked as if out of a magazine. Nothing but quality dining. 

I place four starts because of the first part of my experience but other than that it was a good experience and I I'll come to The Brick again.

We came here on a bustling Saturday. Needless to say, Bricks of Ybor was vacant. A few people were at the bar and some people were sitting outside. The service was subpar and the bartender must have had the worst day of her life. She hated everyone who asked to close their tab. Oh well. I should put a disclaimer that I hate Ybor. It brings me nothing but sorrow.

Yummy food, good vibes, & nice service. Music wasn't too loud. Could hold a conversation without hearing everyone else's. 

I had the Bird & Pig (the way it comes) with the Mac & Cheese. 

I also had the Hukilau. Not a fan. It sounded sweeter than it was. Still giving it a 4 for the food service and atmosphere. It's not their fault I didn't like the alcohol. 

Had a quick bite of the nachos and may have to orders those for the table next visit.

The Bricks has a super cool vibe. I've visited multiple times for dinner and once for drinks. I'm always impressed with their sandwiches and other food. Normally everything is very fresh and tasty. They have a good sized line up of craft beers most of them local to the area, which is something I'm always looking for. 

It's sort of a dive-y location on the outskirts of the main part of Ybor. Late night they have a small menu of appetizers/small plates and have a DJ. It's clientele leads to some awesome people watching. 

All in all, definitely worth a try. It's not super fancy, so it's perfect for a casual dinner or a new place to try to grab a beer (there's a full bar as well).

I went to this place for the first time last Saturday. I just wanted a place to grab some brunch that had mimosas and my friend suggested here. Boy am I glad she did! Besides the crazy run in with a hard core group of strangers doing a running/fitness challenge, the staff there was really really friendly. Our server was very friendly and he even gave us free Appletinis on him! I had the deluxe grilled cheese and it was really really good. The decor was awesome and I'm definitely going back and bringing friends!

This was my first time here and I would recommend it! I had the Liquid Heroin (espresso, chocolate and milk) and the Bird and Pig. These two are the Bricks specialities. The Bird and Pig has chicken, bacon, apple, Brie, and honey. It is a perfect combination of salty and sweet. For dessert, we had the Ice Cream Sammy. A chocolate chip cookie with vanilla bean ice cream and chocolate syrup. I was a bit disappointed on the dessert because I was expecting the cookie to be soft and warm, it was the opposite; very hard. Overall the atmosphere is nice and I would come back to try some of the other specialties they have!
A good watering hole. Beer and coffee are decent! Try UNITA REady Set Gose and UNITA summer ale.

Busy and noisy at 12:30 lunch on a Tuesday.   Quieter by one.  Nice interior gastropub.  My pork and arugala slaw sandwich was good.  It came on a bun that was soft enough to pull apart easily.  When I did so the levels stayed together.  The texture and taste of both the sandwich and the slighly curried potato salad side were good.  I found myself enjoying the overall experience and reluctant to leave.  A good value at less than $10.
It sucks, don't go!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Cold food, stuck up waiters, expensive drinks

Great location, cool atmosphere! The food was a fairly priced for the quality, which was good. I had the pulled pork tacos and they were not skimpy, fully stuffed and filling for $6. Great draft beer selection but it was a buck or two overpriced compared to other craft beer places. The two waitresses were very nice and pleasant. It was slow when we got there and them boom it was packed, they didn't forget about us but we did have to track her down for our last beer. I will be back for sure!

Just came here for cocktails on a Tuesday night. The bar was full but not very busy otherwise. We got the huckle punch and Constantine. The huckleberry vodka in the huckle punch is one of my favorites so loved that drink and the Constantine also very good if you like bourbon! Service was very good and prices were reasonable. Had $3 taco deals and a very cute coffee bar so would definitely be interested in coming back to eat or for a good studying place!

I have to say that the food here is good; however, the staff/service could be better. My sister and I came here for lunch and a few drinks. My sister ordered a drink off the menu and 10+min later, as we're finishing our lunch, the waitress comes back and says "sorry, our bartender doesn't know how to make that" ..... So the bartender doesn't know how to make the drinks listed on the menu? And the 10+mins. it took to tell us that, it could have ben googled and made. I don't want to bash this establishment, but the customer servise has always been an issue here. I would recommend continued training to both current and new staffers to improve their level of knowledge and customer service
1st time we've tried The Bricks. So yummy!!! I had the Blackened Shrimp Salad and my husband had Sammy Tuna. We both loved every bite. Looking forward to eating there again.

My friend and I visited Tampa for a concert, and about ten minutes away from the Atlanta airport he realized that he had purchased tickets for the wrong day. We had already made hotel reservations and bought the concert tickets, so he just had to pay same-day price for airfare: all in all about $800 more. "It was totally worth it," he later told me, "Because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life."

All because we randomly picked the Bricks of Ybor from Yelp. I can't vouch for the peanut butter or meatless menu, but the meat sandwiches that we bought were absolutely phenomenal. I had the pulled pork, which was flavored with ponzu and served on Hawaiian sweet bread. It was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. We spent a few hours hanging out and drinking, during which time Brian, the owner, came out and talked to us, comped us a drink, let us try new appetizers he was developing (all for free) and generally made us feel really welcome. 

I kept my eyes open to the kind of crowd that came in and out of the restaurant. It seemed to draw everything from hipsters to geriatrics and strait-laced families with young kids. I think it speaks to both the diversity of the menu and the pleasant environment. We went back for drinks before and after the concert. It got very crowded but we still received excellent food, drinks and service. I give this restaurant my strongest recommendation, and it's the first place I'm going when I next visit Tampa.
It sucks, don't go!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Cold food, stuck up waiters, expensive drinks

We were greeted by a very pretty waitress that made us feel like we had chosen the right place. We were then turned over to a nice gentleman that took our orders with a polite smile. We are vegetarians and there were lots of options. We settled for the salsa and house made avocado sauce with corn chips and we split their famous black star black bean burger... Yesss!! The food presentation was that of fine dining and the food was very pleasing to our pallets. We give The Bricks 4 stars and would reccomend to anyone who plans to visit Tampa
Really like the Bricks. Always a new experience when i go. The coffee, good. The cocktails, better! The ambiance is hip. The food is pretty good too.

Very fresh food- they actually make their own stuff! We ate lunch at the bar and the bartender went out of his way to help my husband find a good gluten free option. I ordered the black bean burger and it was delishous! Great atmosphere as well. Definitely recomend this place as there are not all that many fresh and relatively healthy places in the area. Wish we had found it sooner!

I ordered the Kung fury bowl and it's pretty good, just not a huge fan of Asian slaw. The restaurant is pretty cool with the decoration and not at a super crowded location in ybor. The service was a bit slow, but the food came pretty quick.

I thoroughly enjoy going to the Bricks. It's unique atmosphere with cheap, but tasty, food options combine for a great experince. The term hipster is thrown around a lot these days and while you may be greeted and surrounded by people in skinny jeans, wearing Toms shoes, IMAX glasses, and an extra piercing, you are treated no differently. I always feel warmly welcomed and entertained. As it does have a large bar, it may get rowdy in the evenings, but the Bricks maintains a family-friendly atmosphere. I ate the Bird and Pig meal once, very very good, and the breakfast bagel the next time. The fiancee had black bean soup and a grilled cheese sandwich. Very tasty combination. Highly recommend!

They seem to have expanded their menu or, I'm just imaging that and actually gave them another chance. Good beer selection. Great ambiance. More hip than some of the other bars. Accommodated my large party.

I loved this place, the food, atmosphere, and drinks and I was in Ybor one night and came in about midnight and walked back to use the restroom and then to sit down and get some food and drinks, typical of anyone that's out drinking and midnight rolls around. Well, I continue on the path to the restroom and the manager, yes, the manager, had the audacity to tell me if I proceeded to the restroom that he would come on after me. I thought he was joking. But no, he was serious, then he told me I needed to tip the bartender before using the restroom, even though I hadn't sat down to order anything yet. I was clearly upset and walked back out to leave. The guy at the door was very nice and lead me back in to use the restroom. I decided after being treated that way, by the manager, that this was not an establishment I would be frequenting any longer, even though I loved the place. I went to the restroom and came back out and put $3 on the bar, because I needed to "tip" to use the restroom. Well, the guy at the door said that the manager had ASSUMED that we came from a rave across the street and that we just wanted to use the restroom. Well, his assumption lost him business, and I have been living in the Bay Area for 32 years. I'm pretty sure telling a patron you are going to follow them into he women's restroom is some form of sexual harassment. I have NEVER been treated like that ever in an establishment. Hopefully, for the greater good of the restaurant, that manager is no longer there.

First of all I would like to say this is a pretty cool place. They have a great selection of beer and booze. The bartenders were very attentive and made awesome drinks. I was there on a Thursday night with a wedding party of about 12 people and we were having a great night. This is where I would love to end this review because based on the atmosphere and bartenders, this is a really chill place to hang out in ybor. Unfortunately, there is more to the story.

Later in the night, the bar started clearing out. The only people in the bar were myself, the wedding party I was with, the bartenders, and 3 other people. That's it. We (the wedding party) thought it would be fun to do the wobble and since the DJ was playing hip-hip anyway, we figured that it wouldn't be an issue to request that he play the wobble. After All, there wasn't many people in the bar anyway. Upon requesting to the DJ that we would like him to play the wobble he proceeded to respond with statements like "I refuse to play that song" "I don't like that song" "I'm not a jukebox". After briefly sharing our differences of opinion, I went to the bar to get a drink. At this time the DJ also walked up to the bar as we were kindly telling the bartender that they might want to reconsider their DJ choices because he was more concerned with what he wanted to hear, rather than what the patrons of the bar wanted to hear. Upon sharing our opinion with the bartender, the DJ butts in again to express that "I'm the DJ, and I'll play what I want to hear" that irritated me and I got a little heated. The bartender proceeded to cut me off because I argued with the DJ. I totally understand that, the bartender did the right thing there to calm down a situation. 

Point of my long story is, I really hope this place reconsiders their DJ choices in the future. They need someone that will play what the patrons want to hear and not what he wants to hear. Maybe that's just my opinion, but I feel that I make a strong case considering that by the time it was all said and done, our party was the only people in the bar. So, instead of 5 stars, I'm marking it a 3 based on the DJ alone.

This is THE BEST spot for food and drinks in Ybor.  The drinks are amazing and the food is top notch. Cool, laid back atmosphere and amazing bar!! All of the staff are helpful and accommodating!! Best happy hour!!!

What an eclectic hipster joint, right in the heart of Ybor. The restaurant name alone fits the atmosphere perfectly. The menu options are unique, what might sound like it wouldn't mesh on the palette ends up making you want seconds and if drinking enough-- thirds. This is a great place to have a drink and a scrumptious sandwich on a Sunday. I had the bird and pig, perfect combination of savory and sweet.
My favorite drinks place to imbibe before a show in Ybor. Kyle is spot on every time with what is seemingly the exact thing I want before I even know it. Also, the nachos. Trust me!
Cute place, got there too late to eat,the drinks were good though, they have fresh ingredients and crushed ice!only bar in ybor I've seen with fresh things and a wide selection of booze

Wanted to try the pig and bird sammich but when I got there I decided on the Pacific Rim. The Asian slaw and bbq theme was too much to pass up. I thought the sandwich was really good and had a nice balance to it. I got chips and queso as my side but with this sandwich fries would have been the go to. They don't have fries so you'll have to choose something else. Service at the bar was really good, there were multiple people that helped me during my meal. One thing is they were out of three of the beers I wanted right off the bat. Pretty cool vibe in the place and people just hanging with friends having drinks and food.

Yummy food, good vibes, & nice service. Music wasn't too loud. Could hold a conversation without hearing everyone else's. I had the Bird & Pig (the way it comes) with the Mac & Cheese. I also had the Hukilau. Not a fan. It sounded sweeter than it was. Still giving it a 4 for the food servise and atmosphere. It's not their fault I didn't like the alcohol. Had a quick bite of the nachos and may have to orders those for the table next visit.

While I was in Tampa for the last 2 years, The Bricks was a second home. Great food and even greater people. I moved back to Seattle and left making friends. Wish I could've brought The Bricks and my new friends back with me. Definitely a place for locals and visitors to check out!
fun place with a nice atmosphere. Ordered the Elvis which is a good sandwich with peanut butter honey bananana and bacon! it sounds weird but it was delicous.
This place is fun! I like the staff and the vibe. Food is okay. Beer selection is okay. Great happy hour on wine once a week. 3.5 stars is more appropriate for this place.

Full disclosure: My experience might just have been an isolated, rare occurrence. I arrived to The Brick and sat myself at the bar. After 15 minutes of zero service I was getting ready to leave but I noticed the waiting staff on the main floor looked active and on top of things. I decided to transition from the lack of service bar to the main floor and, literally, as soon as I sat down I had a waiter hand me a menu, take my drink order and before even a blink I had a Bloody Mary in front on me. Moral of this story, careful sitting at the bar since the service there seemed to be lacking. I'm sure it was the timing since my overall experience was a thumbs up. 

I ordered the loaded Bloody Mary. The drink was simple but very delightful, clearly proving that less is more. The drink had a little satisfying kick that's normal to any Bloody Mary. Overall- very satisfied with their Bloody Mary, so much in fact I ordered two. Maybe a little more body to it but not a must. 

Food: I ordered the Tuna BLT with the side of Asian slaw. Overall: GREAT. The theme here is clearly simple. They exploit every taste which is gratifying since that's the most important thing. The slaw was crisp and surprisingly very refreshing. Now, the tuna can only be described as crafted by a masterful craftsman! Yes, I said it. It tasted better than it looked and that's hard todo since it looked as if out of a magazine. Nothing but quality dining. 

I place four starts because of the first part of my experience but other than that it was a good experience and I I'll come to The Brick again.

I thought the sandwich was really good and had a nice balance to it. I got chips and queso as my side but with this sandwich fries would have been the go to. They don't have fries so you'll have to choose something else. 

Service at the bar was really good, there were multiple people that helped me during my meal. One thing is they were out of three of the beers I wanted right off the bat. 

Pretty cool vibe in the place and people just hanging with friends having drinks and food.

Loved the Mediterranean Grilled Cheese sandwich! Nice casual atmosphere. On the end of the strip so it is very convenient to get to during lunch hour. Looking forward to trying something else on the menu.

I thoroughly enjoy going to the Bricks.  It's unique atmosphere with cheap, but tasty, food options combine for a great experience.  

The term hipster is thrown around a lot these days and while you may be greeted and surrounded by people in skinny jeans, wearing Toms shoes, IMAX glasses, and an extra piercing, you are treated no differently.  I always feel warmly welcomed and entertained.  

As it does have a large bar, it may get rowdy in the evenings, but the Bricks maintains a family-friendly atmosphere.  

I ate the Bird and Pig meal once, very very good, and the breakfast bagel the next time.  The fiancee had black bean soup and a grilled cheese sandwich.  Very tasty combination. 

Highly recommend!

I dig the art and the choices on the menu.

Skanky Chai is pretty good. 

The Elvis was pretty awesome. Peanut butter, bacon, and bananas on cuban toast. 
That sounds a lot like something I would drool over.

Nice!

A couple of nights ago the Tampa Bay Lady Bloggers met at The Bricks for our monthly book club meeting. The staff was very welcoming and was happy to push together several tables for us. Our server was so nice and helpful and cheerfully took a group photo for us (annoying bloggers).

The "hole in the wall" atmosphere at The Bricks is fun and eclectic, with local art for sale lining the walls. I loved the laid-back, hip feeling of the place.

I had the "brick,paper,scissors" martini and it was so refreshing and delicious that I had to get a second with my entree. The table shared an order of the "bricklayer" nachos and they were okay, but the house-made salsa on the side was out of this world. For my entree I got the "bird and pig", based on so many great Yelp recommendations. It did not disappoint with thick, crispy bacon, sweet apples and agave nectar, tasty chicken and delicious pressed "sweet" bread. I almost caved in and got the Ahi tuna BLT because it looked so good on the menu...I'll definitely be back and try that next time to compare.

Thank you Bricks for hosting our meet-up. See you again soon I hope! My blog post about our meeting at The Bricks is here: http://carolinecalcote.com/2012/06/28/tampa-bay-lady-bloggers-book-club/

This was my first time here and I would recommend it! I had the Liquid Heroin (espresso, chocolate and milk) and the Bird and Pig. These two are the Bricks specialities. The Bird and Pig has chicken, bacon, apple, Brie, and honey. It is a perfect combination of salty and sweet. For dessert, we had the Ice Cream Sammy. A chocolate chip cookie with vanilla bean ice cream and chocolate syrup. I was a bit disappointed on the dessert because I was expecting the cookie to be soft and warm, it was the opposite; very hard. Overall the atmosphere is nice and I would come back to try some of the other specialties they have!

Tasty place to grab a unique sandwich or something else with some tasty beer. I love the decor in this restaurant, as it seems to marry bricks, random tomfoolery, and nerdiness quite well. I've enjoyed most things there. The Bird and Pig was quite good as well as their veggie burger. They also have lots of theme nights, but I've never been to one.

If you have ever dreamed of owning a bad ass bar and restaurant, with phenomenal and creative food, solid service, and atmosphere as cool as - well as cool as the bricks in the streets of Ybor City - don't go here. It will be likely to depress you to see that your dream has already been done so well that there just isnt much improvement. 
Well, if there was parking, that would be an improvement - but that's about it. I work nearby and rock their little patio in the back about once a week, it just never disappoints. The CURE is my favorite sandwich but i dont think there are any bad items on the menu - not even the vegetarian ones, and you know how bad those CAN be!

If you are on the west end of Ybor, or staying at the hotels nearby, or just stepped off the streetcar and want to figure out what Ybor City has come to mean these days - the Bricks of Ybor should be your first stop!

I have to say that the food here is good; however, the staff/service could be better. My sister and I came here for lunch and a few drinks. My sister ordered a drink off the menu and 10+min later, as we're finishing our lunch, the waitress comes back and says "sorry, our bartender doesn't know how to make that" ..... So the bartender doesn't know how to make the drinks listed on the menu? And the 10+mins. it took to tell us that, it could have ben googled and made. I don't want to bash this establishment, but the customer service has always been an issue here. I would recommend continued training to both current and new staffers to improve their level of knowledge and customer service

staff is awesome and food is damn good. drinks are a reasonable price and Andrew always has something awesome/weird playing on the TV. If the independent were cooler, it would be the Bricks. 

One of the gods invented the bird and pig. Definitely get that.The cure is pretty tasty too, I'd eat it again. 

The place has cool wall art, a comfortable back patio, and Paper Mario characters on the bathroom doors. Have to appreciate the subtle nerdiness.
My favorite drinks place to imbibe before a show in Ybor. Kyle is spot on every time with what is seemingly the exact thing I want before I even know it. Also, the nachos. Trust me!

One of my favorite places to eat in Ybor! Good vibes, good food, and good drinks. Even their coffee is good! Service is a hit or miss, although most recently I have had consistent great service. And their veggie Cuban sandwich is amaaaazing!

I'd been following the progress of The Bricks via their FB page for some time - I'm happy to report that the end product lives up to the expectations (exceeds them, even!). 

The first thing you notice is the atmosphere: laid-back & friendly, fostering a close-knit/ community feel that encourages you to slow down and linger for a bit longer, enjoying the company. 

When it comes to the menu, it's full of simple foods that have been completely mastered. I suggest the Peanut Butter Bar (choose your bread, peanut butter, and toppers). The Roasted Garlic Hummus is amazing, as is the Italian Brick sandwich. As far as coffee goes - they won't disappoint, I'm partial to the Brickaccino (frozen coffee). Another standout factor is their beer selection - which alone is worth strolling by for.

All in all, The Bricks as a 5-Star stop, you won't soon forget.

I had a good time at The Bricks of Ybor.  The service is really spot on and the quality of the food's pretty good.  I had the pulled pork sandwich.  It was pretty good.  Nothing memorable but what makes this place a four star place are the happy hour beer prices and the interesting art inside.

I loved the star wars art throughout this place and particularly loved the berpo and ern2d2 painting.

Friendly, fun crowd that looks like they're coming to a John Waters costume party.
Came for Father's day brunch, and will definitely come back. great selection of vegetarian food. Veggie Cuban and cheese grits were awesome. .and srvice was so good!
Excellent servise, trendy yet comfortable atmosphere, and very nice food. About half the items we requested weren't available b/c they're transitioning to a new menu.

Lots of vegetarian options. The service was pretty fast. The skateboard wall was nice (Calvin & Hobbes represent!). The sandwich I got was a bit lacking in the flavor department. Really didn't know what to eat since I went here at night just before a binge of dancing and drinking. Didn't really feel into the peanut butter at that point in time. Next time I'll try their peanut butter creations, but I'll probably go for brunch or a late lunch since it seems the menu is more designed for that and not any pre-gaming.

Where do i start with this place!
I love that they have local art on the walls/ always doing art shows 

the staff that works there always rocking smiles talking to all the guess a all around good atmosphere vibe

I tip my hat to the head chef (Chef Ben) The food is always on point and i like when the cooks yell "ORDER UP" hahaha 

I can wright a book about how awesome this place is 

KEEP UP THE GOOD WORK and SEE YOU SOON!

I ordered the Kung fury bowl and it's pretty good, just not a huge fan of Asian slaw. The restaurant is pretty cool with the decoration and not at a super crowded location in ybor. The service was a bit slow, but the food came pretty quick.

Either ate or had drinks here a few times over the summer as my office was just upstairs. I'm not a vegetarian, but the Goodness wrap is a knockout. I also greatly enjoyed the chili I had here, though it was a special so I'm not sure how often it comes around. I'm not really into the hipster vibe of the staff, but I never had any service problems and that's what is most important. I definitely don't live or die by The Bricks but it's a place I would suggest if you're ever in Ybor City.

One of my favorite places to eat in Ybor! Good vibes, good food, and good drinks. Even their coffee is good! Service is a hit or miss, although most recently I have had consistent great service. And their veggie Cuban sandwich is amaaaazing!

First of all I would like to say this is a pretty cool place. They have a great selection of beer and booze. The bartenders were very attentive and made awesome drinks. I was there on a Thursday night with a wedding party of about 12 people and we were having a great night. This is where I would love to end this review because based on the atmosphere and bartenders, this is a really chill place to hang out in ybor. Unfortunately, there is more to the story.

Later in the night, the bar started clearing out. The only people in the bar were myself, the wedding party I was with, the bartenders, and 3 other people. That's it. We (the wedding party) thought it would be fun to do the wobble and since the DJ was playing hip-hip anyway, we figured that it wouldn't be an issue to request that he play the wobble. After All, there wasn't many people in the bar anyway. Upon requesting to the DJ that we would like him to play the wobble he proceeded to respond with statements like "I refuse to play that song" "I don't like that song" "I'm not a jukebox". After briefly sharing our differences of opinion, I went to the bar to get a drink. At this time the DJ also walked up to the bar as we were kindly telling the bartender that they might want to reconsider their DJ choices because he was more concerned with what he wanted to hear, rather than what the patrons of the bar wanted to hear. Upon sharing our opinion with the bartender, the DJ butts in again to express that "I'm the DJ, and I'll play what I want to hear" that irritated me and I got a little heated. The bartender proceeded to cut me off because I argued with the DJ. I totally understand that, the bartender did the right thing there to calm down a situation. 

Point of my long story is, I really hope this place reconsiders their DJ choices in the future. They need someone that will play what the patrons want to hear and not what he wants to hear. Maybe that's just my opinion, but I feel that I make a strong case considering that by the time it was all said and done, our party was the only people in the bar. So, instead of 5 stars, I'm marking it a 3 based on the DJ alone.

Their bird & pig sandwich is the bomb. Brie cheese is one of my favs and this sandwich offers plenty. The Asian Slaw was a suggestion from our waitress and did not disappoint. It was yummy. The sesame seeds made all the difference. Full bar always has a variety of tasty drink options. This place is cool bc it has a vegan options for those folks with those dietary needs.

The Bricks is a hipster haven, but don't let that deter you if you don't wear non-prescription glasses and flannel. I'm always the least cool person in here and no one seems to mind. (Although maybe I AM cool -- last time I was here the DJ was playing Hall & Oates most likely to be ironic, but I genuinely enjoyed it.) The menu is mostly sandwiches and some salads. It's all about the Bird & Pig sandwich. I have a hard time straying from this delicacy of chicken, bacon, brie, and apples on pressed sweet bread. Sweet, check. Salty, check. Crunchy, check. Nice selection of local and craft brews, too.

This was my first time here and I would recommend it! I had the Liquid Heroin (espresso, chocolate and milk) and the Bird and Pig. These two are the Bricks specialities. The Bird and Pig has chicken, bacon, apple, Brie, and honey. It is a perfect combination of salty and sweet. For dessert, we had the Ice Cream Sammy. A chocolate chip cookie with vanilla bean ice cream and chocolate syrup. I was a bit disappointed on the dessert because I was expecting the cookie to be soft and warm, it was the opposite; very hard. Overall the atmosphere is nice and I would come back to try some of the other specialties they have!

This place is listed as vegetarian-friendly and it is, provided that you eat eggs, cheese, and whatever else they put on the food without listing it in the menu description. Unfortunately this place was a nightmare for me as a vegan. I ordered the veggie cuban with no swiss or honey mustard since those were the only non-vegan ingredients listed in the description, and if it wasn't for the server mentioning "oh that's a great choice; the chef puts an egg on it too," then I would have gotten a sandwich with egg. After I stressed "no animal products, no egg, no dairy, no butter," the server responded with "oh well you know the egg isn't actually meat" as opposed to, you know, respecting my dietary restrictions.

I have no intention of returning, due to the lack of clarity on the menu and the server's rudeness when I was expressing my allergies/restrictions. Maybe if the restaurant lists all of the ingredients and trains their staff on how to not be rude to someone who was rightfully annoyed at almost getting an item I couldn't eat, then it might be worth a recommendation. But then again, it's not a vegan-friendly establishment despite it being vegetarian-friendly.

fun place with a nice atmosphere. Ordered the Elvis which is a good sandwich with peanut butter honey bananana and bacon! it sounds weird but it was delicious.

Seems like a good place ...very chill and low key..not my particular favorite food ( more on the healthy side) but still good quality food and service with a fun video game theme once a week ...good place to check out

Visited The Bricks this evening for dinner with a group of 6 and I think I can say we all enjoyed our experience  - I give it a solid 3-stars because I wasn't blown away by the food, ambiance or service but all were good if not a little above average. 

I started with an Old Fashioned which was sadly, quite watered down.  The table started with the Bricklayer Nachos which were good and a pretty decent size portion too.  For my dinner I had the Mediterranean Grilled Cheese - feta and mozzarella cheese, olive tapenade, baby spinach and portabello mushroom pressed in a piece of flatbread.  The first few bites were enjoyable but about a quarter of the way into it I realized how SALTY it was.  Unfortunately, it was a little one-note and better in concept than in execution in my opinion. 

Our waitress was pleasant and split the check 6-ways without us even having to ask, which I thought was really nice of her.  Atmosphere was unique but nothing worth coming back for.

Also, worth noting - The Bricks doesn't have its own parking lot so you'll have to find street parking (good luck), a paid parking lot lot or one of the local parking garages.
