I went to this place for the first time last Saturday. I just wanted a place to grab some brunch that had mimosas and my friend suggested here. Boy am I glad she did!

Besides the crazy run in with a hard core group of strangers doing a running/fitness challenge, the staff there was really really friendly. Our server was very friendly and he even gave us free Appletinis on him!

I had the deluxe grilled cheese and it was really really good. 

The decor was awesome and I'm definitely going back and bringing friends!

A couple of nights ago the Tampa Bay Lady Bloggers met at The Bricks for our monthly book club meeting. The staff was very welcoming and was happy to push together several tables for us. Our server was so nice and helpful and cheerfully took a group photo for us (annoying bloggers). The "hole in the wall" atmosphere at The Bricks is fun and eclectic, with local art for sale lining the walls. I loved the laid-back, hip feeling of the place. I had the "brick,paper,scissors" martini and it was so refreshing and deliciuos that I had to get a second with my entree. The table shared an order of the "bricklayer" nachos and they were okay, but the house-made salsa on the side was out of this world. For my entree I got the "bird and pig", based on so many great Yelp recommendations. It did not disappoint with thick, crispy bacon, sweet apples and agave nectar, tasty chicken and delicious pressed "sweet" bread. I almost caved in and got the Ahi tuna BLT because it looked so good on the menu...I'll definately be back and try that next time to compare. Thank you Bricks for hosting our meet-up. See you again soon I hope! My blog post about our meeting at The Bricks is here: http://carolinecalcote.com/2012/06/28/tampa-bay-lady-bloggers-book-club/
Excellent service, trendy yet comfortable atmosphere, and very nice food. About half the items we requested weren't available b/c they're transitioning to a new menu.

My friend and I visited Tampa for a concert, and about ten minutes away from the Atlanta airport he realized that he had purchased tickets for the wrong day. We had already made hotel reservations and bought the concert tickets, so he just had to pay same-day price for airfare: all in all about $800 more. "It was totally worth it," he later told me, "Because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life." All because we randomly picked the Bricks of Ybor from Yelp. I can't vouch for the peanut butter or meatless menu, but the meat sandwiches that we bought were absolutely phenomenal. I had the pulled pork, which was flavored with ponzu and served on Hawaiian sweet bread. It was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. We spent a few hours hanging out and drinking, during which time Brian, the owner, came out and talked to us, comped us a drink, let us try new appetizers he was developing (all for free) and generally made us feel really welcome. I kept my eyes open to the kind of crowd that came in and out of the restaurant. It seemed to draw everything from hipsters to geriatrics and strait-laced families with young kids. I think it speaks to both the diversity of the menu and the pleasant environment. We went back for drinks before and after the concert. It got very crowded but we still received excellent food, drinks and srvice. I give this restraunt my strongest recommendation, and it's the first place I'm going when I next visit Tampa.

We waited an hour for our food.  No coffee refills the entire time.  We saw our food souring in the window for 20 minutes.  When we finally left the server said it couldn't be helped.  No apologies, no service, no food, no tip.

Great environment, good assortments of beers, funky people, board games, chill vibes, Monday Game nights and random parties, outside patio, great coffee, try liquid heroin coffee, one of my favorite places in town

My 2 favorite guy friends and I came here for Valentine's Day this year! I love everything about this place.  Every time I have visited there has been a friendly/diverse crowd and good music. I really like the atmosphere and the local artwork that is displayed throughout the restaurant. I highly recommend the brick layer nachos! My friends and I ate every bite and I honestly will most likely order that as my meal next time. The night we visited they had 50% off bottles of wine and after splitting the cost with one of my friends it was only $7 (need I say more?).  I ordered the brick layer salad with tuna for my meal. I ordered something lighter due to my massive nacho intake and the salad was good but it was similar to a house salad you can get anywhere. They have a very eclectic menu and next time I will probably try one of the many grilled cheese sandwiches listed on the menu. I will definitely be back!

The Bricks completely lives up to the hype. Don't leave without trying their amazing Basil-infused lemonade!

Really chill cafe-like vibe, with a creative comfort food menu (peanut butter sandwiches!), and full table service.

In a few weeks they will be opening a quiet "study hall" space for laptop lurkers, making this a killer telecommute/study spot.

First of all I would like to say this is a pretty cool place. They have a great selection of beer and booze. The bartenders were very attentive and made awesome drinks. I was there on a Thursday night with a wedding party of about 12 people and we were having a great night. This is where I would love to end this review because based on the atmosphere and bartenders, this is a really chill place to hang out in ybor. Unfortunately, there is more to the story. Later in the night, the bar started clearing out. The only people in the bar were myself, the wedding party I was with, the bartenders, and 3 other people. That's it. We (the wedding party) thought it would be fun to do the wobble and since the DJ was playing hip-hip anyway, we figured that it wouldn't be an issue to request that he play the wobble. After All, there wasn't many people in the bar anyway. Upon requesting to the DJ that we would like him to play the wobble he proceeded to respond with statements like "I refuse to play that song" "I don't like that song" "I'm not a jukebox". After briefly sharing our differences of opinion, I went to the bar to get a drink. At this time the DJ also walked up to the bar as we were kindly telling the bartender that they might want to reconsider their DJ choices because he was more concerned with what he wanted to hear, rather than what the patrons of the bar wanted to hear. Upon sharing our opinion with the bartender, the DJ butts in again to express that "I'm the DJ, and I'll play what I want to hear" that irritated me and I got a little heated. The bartender proceeded to cut me off because I argued with the DJ. I totally understand that, the bartender did the right thing there to calm down a situation. Point of my long story is, I really hope this place reconsiders their DJ choices in the future. They need someone that will play what the patrons want to hear and not what he wants to hear. Maybe that's just my opinion, but I feel that I make a strong case considering that by the time it was all said and done, our party was the only people in the bar. So, instead of 5 stars, I'm marking it a 3 based on the DJ alone.
It's a beer pub so don't go to eat a meal. Beer was great but not all of them were available at the time I visited [April] so....??

How can you not like this place? Fresh water upon arrival followed by healthy food with a twist. The service has always been exemplary so no complaints there. This is one of the few joints in Tampa that can appease an array of crowds - hipsters love the decor, drink selections, etc.; geriatrics enjoy the healthy food portions, friendliness, etc.; and out-of-towners relish the overall uniqueness of the place. This is beyond highly recommended.

Wanted to try the pig and bird sammich but when I got there I decided on the Pacific Rim. The Asian slaw and bbq theme was too much to pass up. I thought the sandwich was really good and had a nice balance to it. I got chips and queso as my side but with this sandwich fries would have been the go to. They don't have fries so you'll have to choose something else. 

Service at the bar was really good, there were multiple people that helped me during my meal. One thing is they were out of three of the beers I wanted right off the bat. 

Pretty cool vibe in the place and people just hanging with friends having drinks and food.

If you're immune to salmonella poisoning then this is the perfect place for you! Very overpriced, minimum effort in providing authentic food NOT out of a can. They undercook the chicken and it taste like refrigerator. Please don't waste your hard earned cash on half assed food. Unless you just want drinks and a good time with friends, don't come here.

This is more of a drinking place than dinner. I didn't enjoy dining here at all, the service was slow and the acoustics of the place made It impossible to have a conversation. The veggie cubano was pretty good and the drinks were strong though.
Great atmosphere and service, food and drinks were excellent. Everything was fresh.  Bird and the pig sandwich was delicious, also the pacific rim. Will return soon.
My favorite drinks place to imbibe before a show in Ybor. Kyle is spot on every time with what is seemingly the exact thing I want before I even know it. Also, the nachos. Trust me!

The Bricks has a super cool vibe. I've visited multiple times for dinner and once for drinks. I'm always impressed with their sandwiches and other food. Normally everything is very fresh and tasty. They have a good sized line up of craft beers most of them local to the area, which is something I'm always looking for. 

It's sort of a dive-y location on the outskirts of the main part of Ybor. Late night they have a small menu of appetizers/small plates and have a DJ. It's clientele leads to some awesome people watching. 

All in all, definitely worth a try. It's not super fancy, so it's perfect for a casual dinner or a new place to try to grab a beer (there's a full bar as well).

I went there for dinner while in the Tampa area and had a great meal. They have multiple Vegan and Vegetarian options, while also having a full bar with Guinness. Very unusual across the good ole USA. The place is in an interesting area, which seems it could be a little rough in the dark, so if you go, I would recomend going during the light hours. The bartenders are really nice, and helpful with picking a good dish.

They seem to have expanded their menu or, I'm just imaging that and actually gave them another chance. Good beer selection. Great ambiance. More hip than some of the other bars. Accommodated my large party.
Great bar/café! Such a great place to hang, inside is beautiful and outside you can hear nice music while having a coffee and a cig! Definitely coming back! Loved it

1st time we've tried The Bricks. So yummy!!! I had the Blackened Shrimp Salad and my husband had Sammy Tuna. We both loved every bite. Looking forward to eating there again.

We came here on a bustling Saturday. Needless to say, Bricks of Ybor was vacant. A few people were at the bar and some people were sitting outside. The service was subpar and the bartender must have had the worst day of her life. She hated everyone who asked to close their tab. Oh well. 

I should put a disclaimer that I hate Ybor. It brings me nothing but sorrow.
I love this place. Everything I've had seems really fresh. The hummus is really tasty and the ambiance is nice and relaxed.

I walk in, and they're playing the greatest hits of De La Soul throughout lunch. They could have been serving Big Macs and that gets you four stars alone. 

I order a grilled cheese sandwich, and it comes with apple, plums, and bacon on some delicious bread with tortilla chips. And it is sublime. The cheese is perfectly melted, and the goodies inside are covered in wonderful gooey dairy greatness. 

I order a cafe con leche while getting some work done on my laptop. It is flawlessly prepared by a lovely server, and I'm a coffee snob. And if I didn't get buried in work stuff, I was jonesing for one of those half-price martinis they serve on Thursdays.

Wonderful atmosphere (the skatepark staff makes it friendly and fun), great food, delicious coffee, a full bar, and lots of different options. This place is a total home run, and a can't miss for anyone in Ybor.

We went at a slow time on a weekday afternoon for a late lunch because we were all wanting sandwiches. So between us all we had: the Bird & Pig, BBQ quesadilla, ahi BLT, clubhouse and kids pbj. All the sandwiches were great! Service was a bit slow though. If I was in the area again I may try again but I would not go out of my way to eat here.

I had high expectations when I went to this place recently after some recommendations from friends.  We visited on a night when there weren't very crowded so it was nice to be able to have such an attentive waitress and service.  I was a bit disappointed when I didn't find as much on the menu as I would have liked to have seen that would appeal to me.  I guess I have become very picky with my Yelp addiction in terms of scrutinizing every establishment I go to pretty thoroughly.  

I ordered the hummus appetizer for the table and was very pleased at the quality of the dish.  For my entree I ordered their Bricks Salad which had plenty of fresh produce packed in.  I ordered a double portion of chicken for it, which still seemed pretty skimpy especially since I was charged for that request.  Overall, I'd say this is probably one of Ybor's lesser known spots as its more on the western edge of the main strip, yet it seems very lively and upbeat.  I did like that they had featured lots of artwork by various local artists that were on display and offerred for sale.  Not a bad place to hang out and have a drink if you're looking for a lower key outing in the Ybor area.

My wife and I have visited twice, and another time with friends. While we like the food and beer choices, the service is inexcusably very slow. We visited on a Saturday afternoon around 5:00 and the place was only 1/3 full. Took a while for our server to greet us, arrived just when we were about to get up and leave. Ordered a beer for each of us and waited at least 10 minutes before I finally got up to ask the bartender about our drinks (after watching him not making any drinks for several minutes and serving a few others who just arrived at the bar). I could barely get the words out before he says they'll be right up. I sit back down, and he still doesn't pour them. We were about to leave again when another bartender made eye contact and she poured the drinks and brought them to us. While our waitress was friendly, she should have been checking on our drinks. Same slow experience with the other two visits, this time we are certain we will not be back.

A good watering hole. Beer and coffee are decent!  Try UNITA REady Set Gose and UNITA summer ale.

We've heard that we need to go to places in Ybor and try them out, so we set out to find a place for dinner.  One thing is for sure...the menu has traditional food, but in a unique way.  

I ordered the deluxe grilled cheese (has tomatoes, pesto, whole wheat) and my husband had the BBQ pig quesadilla.  Both dishes were good, but I don't feel like they were 'awesome'.  

We went out on a limb and tried the hibiscus sangria and the chocolate espresso cake for dessert.  The cake was VERY espresso!  Too rich for me!  The sangria definitely tasted like flowers, but in a good way. It was pretty refreshing too!

 It was fun to try a new place, but I don't think we'll go back.

Full disclosure: My experience might just have been an isolated, rare occurrence. I arrived to The Brick and sat myself at the bar. After 15 minutes of zero service I was getting ready to leave but I noticed the waiting staff on the main floor looked active and on top of things. I decided to transition from the lack of service bar to the main floor and, literally, as soon as I sat down I had a waiter hand me a menu, take my drink order and before even a blink I had a Bloody Mary in front on me. Moral of this story, careful sitting at the bar since the service there seemed to be lacking. I'm sure it was the timing since my overall experience was a thumbs up. 

I ordered the loaded Bloody Mary. The drink was simple but very delightful, clearly proving that less is more. The drink had a little satisfying kick that's normal to any Bloody Mary. Overall- very satisfied with their Bloody Mary, so much in fact I ordered two. Maybe a little more body to it but not a must. 

Food: I ordered the Tuna BLT with the side of Asian slaw. Overall: GREAT. The theme here is clearly simple. They exploit every taste which is gratifying since that's the most important thing. The slaw was crisp and surprisingly very refreshing. Now, the tuna can only be described as crafted by a masterful craftsman! Yes, I said it. It tasted better than it looked and that's hard todo since it looked as if out of a magazine. Nothing but quality dining. 

I place four starts because of the first part of my experience but other than that it was a good experience and I I'll come to The Brick again.
This place is fun! I like the staff and the vibe. Food is okay. Beer selection is okay. Great happy hour on wine once a week. 3.5 stars is more appropriate for this place.
Great bar/café! Such a great place to hang, inside is beautiful and outside you can hear nice music while having a coffee and a cig! Definitely coming back! Loved it
Easily my favorite overall spot in Ybor. The food is freaking amazing, the staff is awesome and know their booze/beer, and it just has a great feel.
It's a beer pub so don't go to eat a meal. Beer was great but not all of them were available at the time I visited [April] so....??

For days I have tried to put a side the terrible experience I had, I really don't like to put a bad review, but most of all I deeply appreciate when businesses treat everyone with respect and priority, and for some reason and actually for no reason.
I walked in and noticed I have to go to the bar for service, there were no available seats, so I stood at the beginning of the bar from the entrance, made an eye contact with the bar tender, 5 min passed he still didn't come to me so I looked over for a menu and grabbed it myself, shortly after he reached to me and took my order of drinks and food... 10 min passed and he didn't prepare my drinks, he left the bar area, and another guy came to replace him, he asked us if we needed help, I told him we already ordered, mean while I'm waiting and waiting and I see our server went to take out food for people, totally forgot about us, he could have at least tell the other two guys who were at the bar ( one of them was the owner) to make us the drink...
Then the owner came to me and he told me I should have told the guy that replaced him to make me the drinks, i told him how could I know it works that way?
And instead of trying to make excuses for why I don't have my drinks and blaming me for it, he obviously didn't care for what u had to say but I tried explain him how long I've been waiting and that I should have been taken care off and that he's been very rude for trying to excuse the situation instead of handling It property...
End of story, He got mad he said I'm the owner and that I'm not going to talk to him that way and he walked away from me!


So to sum it all up, I waited a while until I was served, the tender argued with me that chocolate always has milk inside ( just a lack of knowledge) the owner saw us waiting and waiting , looked at us while serving others, and than he got the nerve to be mad at me for being upset....!!!!

Food is terrible. Nacho dip was covered in there advacado cream dressing which was bad. Very sloppy. The pesto grilled cheese, was covered in way too much pesto. Again very sloppy. Overall bad food, chef must be high or something. Oh and found a few ants crawling up my leg. Will never come back.

I'd been following the progress of The Bricks via their FB page for some time - I'm happy to report that the end product lives up to the expectations (exceeds them, even!). 

The first thing you notice is the atmosphere: laid-back & friendly, fostering a close-knit/ community feel that encourages you to slow down and linger for a bit longer, enjoying the company. 

When it comes to the menu, it's full of simple foods that have been completely mastered. I suggest the Peanut Butter Bar (choose your bread, peanut butter, and toppers). The Roasted Garlic Hummus is amazing, as is the Italian Brick sandwich. As far as coffee goes - they won't disappoint, I'm partial to the Brickaccino (frozen coffee). Another standout factor is their beer selection - which alone is worth strolling by for.

All in all, The Bricks as a 5-Star stop, you won't soon forget.

This place is listed as vegetarian-friendly and it is, provided that you eat eggs, cheese, and whatever else they put on the food without listing it in the menu description. Unfortunately this place was a nightmare for me as a vegan. I ordered the veggie cuban with no swiss or honey mustard since those were the only non-vegan ingredients listed in the description, and if it wasn't for the server mentioning "oh that's a great choice; the chef puts an egg on it too," then I would have gotten a sandwich with egg. After I stressed "no animal products, no egg, no dairy, no butter," the server responded with "oh well you know the egg isn't actually meat" as opposed to, you know, respecting my dietary restrictions.

I have no intention of returning, due to the lack of clarity on the menu and the server's rudeness when I was expressing my allergies/restrictions. Maybe if the restaurant lists all of the ingredients and trains their staff on how to not be rude to someone who was rightfully annoyed at almost getting an item I couldn't eat, then it might be worth a recommendation. But then again, it's not a vegan-friendly establishment despite it being vegetarian-friendly.

We were greeted by a very pretty waitress that made us feel like we had chosen the right place. We were then turned over to a nice gentleman that took our orders with a polite smile. We are vegetarians and there were lots of options. We settled for the salsa and house made avocado sauce with corn chips  and we split their famous black star black bean burger... Yesss!! The food presentation was that of fine dining and the food was very pleasing to our pallets. 
We give The Bricks 4 stars and would recommend to anyone who plans to visit Tampa

We went at a slow time on a weekday afternoon for a late lunch because we were all wanting sandwiches. So between us all we had: the Bird & Pig, BBQ quesadilla, ahi BLT, clubhouse and kids pbj. All the sandwiches were great! Service was a bit slow though. If I was in the area again I may try again but I would not go out of my way to eat here.
Great bar/café! Such a great place to hang, inside is beautiful and outside you can hear nice music while having a coffee and a cig! Definitely coming back! Loved it

While I was in Tampa for the last 2 years, The Bricks was a second home. Great food and even greater people. I moved back to Seattle and left making friends. Wish I could've brought The Bricks and my new friends back with me. Definitely a place for locals and visitors to check out!

They seem to have expanded their menu or, I'm just imaging that and actually gave them another chance. Good beer selection. Great ambiance. More hip than some of the other bars. Accommodated my large party.

Food is terrible. Nacho dip was covered in there advacado cream dressing which was bad. Very sloppy. The pesto grilled cheese, was covered in way too much pesto. Again very sloppy. Overall bad food, chef must be high or something. Oh and found a few ants crawling up my leg. 
Will never come back.

Either ate or had drinks here a few times over the summer as my office was just upstairs.  I'm not a vegetarian, but the Goodness wrap is a knockout.  I also greatly enjoyed the chili I had here, though it was a special so I'm not sure how often it comes around.  I'm not really into the hipster vibe of the staff, but I never had any service problems and that's what is most important.  

I definitely don't live or die by The Bricks but it's a place I would suggest if you're ever in Ybor City.

Lots of vegetarian options. The service was pretty fast. The skateboard wall was nice (Calvin & Hobbes represent!). The sandwich I got was a bit lacking in the flavor department. Really didn't know what to eat since I went here at night just before a binge of dancing and drinking. Didn't really feel into the peanut butter at that point in time. Next time I'll try their peanut butter creations, but I'll probably go for brunch or a late lunch since it seems the menu is more designed for that and not any pre-gaming.

2 words THE CURE! I ended up here after a night of one too many drinks (it happens). A friend recommended this place for a hang over cure! She was not mistaken! After reviewing their menu, which seemed a bit obnoxious, (I'm talking quirky names that require you read the description to be able to decipher what you're eating) I settled on the sandwich with an egg on it! Im a sucker for a runny egg on just about anything! Messy eggs, bacon, mozzarella, jalapeño aioli, on toasted cuban bread; this holy grail of a sandwich is called THE CURE! I have been back a few times to this establishment just for this sandwich, the mimosas too. Oh yea they have liquor so you can totally have drinks here. 

The ambience is very chill. There are a good amount of tables inside and bar seating; no outside seating. I have been here on a Sunday for brunch and found it to be pretty family/kid friendly. The whole place and most of the staff is painfully hipster but it works. The bathrooms are clean and there is a small back patio with mural art.

Since moving to Tampa about three weeks ago, I have found some ridiculously good restaurants thanks to Yelp and friends' recommendations. 

The Bricks has been on my list of places to try for a while now, and I finally made it last night. 

My friend & I walked in and were greeted immediately by the staff who told us to sit where we wanted. The place was fairly empty on a Tuesday at 7pm. I've heard it's packed on weekends, so perhaps going on off-nights is key. 

We started off with the Bricklayer, a fancy name for extra delicious nachos that are topped with queso, avocado cream, olives, and jalapeños. The salsa that comes on the side is awesome - super fresh, flavorful, and not too watery. This is a big appetizer and probably a bit too much for two girls before dinner. If I ordered it again, it would be as a bar snack rather than an app. 

For dinner, I had to try the Bird & the Pig. Wow - that pressed sweet bread combined with the salty bacon and chicken, paired with crisp apples and agave nectar? Yeah, the distinct flavors come together nicely to create one hell of a sandwich. 

I tasted my friend's black bean burger and liked that, too. 

The only thing I tasted that didn't blow me away was the roasted potato salad I got on the side. I'll probably just go with the mixed greens salad next time. 

Aside from the food, the environment is cool, too. I really liked all the local artists' work adorning the walls. 

There is ample parking nearby, including a garage on 15th that only charges $1 for the first 3 hours.
nice place for gatherings and hanging out. Friendly staff. Food was OK. Not bad, not good, it just sat somewhere in the middle.

Have come to The Bricks a few times as I wait for classes, there is wifi and it's a nice environment to sit, eat, grab a beer and do some homework.  If I'm in Ybor for an extended period of time and have to wait, I usually try to make it here as much as I can.
fun place with a nice atmosphere. Ordered the Elvis which is a good sandwich with peanut butter honey bananana and bacon! it sounds weird but it was delicious.

I like some of the cocktails here but the food is mediocre. Ive never understood why it gets the ratings on food that it does, but then again we are in Tampa. Its basically like food you could whip up in a few minutes at home using your microwave for a 3rd of the cost. Except not as tasty. Anyone who loves eating here has the palate of a 14-year-old boy. Maybe its time they get an actual kitchen.

The Bricks of Ybor is a restaurant, bar, and coffee bar in Ybor City and also has live music and special events at times. It is affiliated with the SkatePark of Tampa (SpoT) which has a shop next door and there are skateboard decks mounted on the walls of The Bricks as artwork and they play skate videos on the TVs above the bar; as I'm a skater myself, this is if anything just the icing on the cake for me. 

However, The Bricks' ardent support of skateboarding would not be enough to garner a five-star review alone, but thankfully it measures up in all other regards. The interior atmosphere is lively, inviting, and unique. The waitstaff and bartenders are on point, outgoing, friendly, and most importantly, quite prompt. As to the food, it's fairly simply fare but very tasty and very well-prepared. Tacos, a variety of Cuban sandwich variants, and some salads compose the lion's share of the menu. I had the Bird & Pig Cuban sandwich and also an order of chips and queso dip. The queso was especially good, which impressed me because too often things like queso are simply after-thoughts at bar-type restaurants. The sandwich itself was also very good. They have a full bar with a good selection of bourbons and ryes and also an expectedly good selection of beer, with an emphasis on Tampa's local brews. The wine list also looked better than you'd think for a casual bar atmosphere. Overall, it's clear they're investing in quality here. 

While their skateboarding association was enough to grab my attention to The Bricks, their stellar food and service are what really sets them apart. Ybor has a reputation for food being hit or miss, as is the case with many touristy areas, but The Bricks I found to be simply and casual yet truly impressive.

It was so difficult deciding what to order here. I was in the mood for a skanky chai latte, but the skinny bitch latte just had that calorie conscious ring to it.

After a bit of thought I decided, skanky it shall be!

This has got to be one of my favorite places in Tampa. I had never really put a pulse on "hipster" in Tampa, but I found the closest thing to it at Bricks. Plenty of space to lounge here with a nice offering that ranged from caffeinated beverages to brews and snacks.

I would have never typically thought to throw bacon on a peanut butter and banana sandwich and then drizzle with honey, but I'm glad someone did.
The Elvis sandwich is a hunka, hunka, burning yum!

I would give this place five stars all day, except for the fact that service is slow. Like, dial-up slow. Like larvae to butterfly metamorphosis slow. So slow in fact that on a pretty *slow* afternoon, it would take 20 minutes just to get an iced chai even though you have a clear view of queue and activity of the servers. So slow that from time of check request to actually receiving it, was about another 20 minutes.

While the laid back atmosphere is one of the things that makes this place so cool, it's also the incredibly laid back service that could put a damper on things if you're in a rush.

Busy and noisy at 12:30 lunch on a Tuesday.   Quieter by one.  Nice interior gastropub.  My pork and arugala slaw sandwich was good.  It came on a bun that was soft enough to pull apart easily.  When I did so the levels stayed together.  The texture and taste of both the sandwich and the slighly curried potato salad side were good.  I found myself enjoying the overall experience and reluctant to leave.  A good value at less than $10.

We waited an hour for our food. No coffee refills the entire time. We saw our food souring in the window for 20 minutes. When we finally left the server said it couldn't be helped. No apologies, no service, no food, no tip.

I thoroughly enjoy going to the Bricks.  It's unique atmosphere with cheap, but tasty, food options combine for a great experience.  

The term hipster is thrown around a lot these days and while you may be greeted and surrounded by people in skinny jeans, wearing Toms shoes, IMAX glasses, and an extra piercing, you are treated no differently.  I always feel warmly welcomed and entertained.  

As it does have a large bar, it may get rowdy in the evenings, but the Bricks maintains a family-friendly atmosphere.  

I ate the Bird and Pig meal once, very very good, and the breakfast bagel the next time.  The fiancee had black bean soup and a grilled cheese sandwich.  Very tasty combination. 

Highly recommend!
My favorite drinks place to imbibe before a show in Ybor. Kyle is spot on every time with what is seemingly the exact thing I want before I even know it. Also, the nachos. Trust me!
I love this place.  Everything I've had seems really fresh.  The hummus is really tasty and the ambiance is nice and relaxed.
Great, laid-back atmosphere, terrific food. The ahi was good quality, as were the hummus and curry dip. We're going back for the peanut butter sandwiches.

Leaving this 2-star review in response to the food, not the place as a drinking/hangout spot...although the wine was crap, too. 2-Stars awarded for the Nintendo 64 and all of the nostalgia-worthy games, the decent choice of drafts (even if they were out of the draft I ordered), and the great service from the staff. The food, on the other hand, will make you wish you had eaten at home. My wife and I went out as a treat because we didn't feel like cooking, but the majority of our food was sub-par. I got the shrimp po-boy which was not a po-boy by definition (it was just shrimp on a crappy sandwich...no French bread, no Cajun sauce or even enough Cajun seasoning, and the shrimp was obviously frozen-thawed not fresh). One of the shrimps was even gray when I bit into it, and the sandwich itself smelled more like old fish than fresh shrimp. My wife got the Athena chicken sandwich and that was just so-so, with the overwhelming taste of feta disguising the low-quality factory chicken they use for the sandwich. The best part of our collective meals was the mixed greens we ordered as a side, so I wouldn't exactly recommend ordering food here unless you're completely hammered and taste is not a priority.

How can you not like this place? Fresh water upon arrival followed by healthy food with a twist. The service has always been exemplary so no complaints there. This is one of the few joints in Tampa that can appease an array of crowds - hipsters love the decor, drink selections, etc.; geriatrics enjoy the healthy food portions, friendliness, etc.; and out-of-towners relish the overall uniqueness of the place. This is beyond highly recommended.

It will be likely to depress you to see that your dream has already been done so well that there just isnt much improvement.

The CURE is my favorite sandwich but i dont think there are any bad items on the menu - not even the vegetarian ones, and you know how bad those CAN be!

I'm not either but I do love that black bean burger and the salads are to die for.
The staff is great and always sweet and accommodating.

Yup! Just referred to myself as a cool kid.:D

The Bricks is a tasty restaurant for lunch with a cool and unique Ybor City atmosphere along with friendly service! The only reason it didn't get 5 stars is because it is a little pricey for the quantities.

Loved the Mediterranean Grilled Cheese sandwich! Nice casual atmosphere. On the end of the strip so it is very convenient to get to during lunch hour. Looking forward to trying something else on the menu.
Easily my favorite overall spot in Ybor. The food is freaking amazing, the staff is awesome and know their booze/beer, and it just has a great feel.

Wanted to try the pig and bird sammich but when I got there I decided on the Pacific Rim. The Asian slaw and bbq theme was too much to pass up. I thought the sandwich was really good and had a nice balance to it. I got chips and queso as my side but with this sandwich fries would have been the go to. They don't have fries so you'll have to choose something else. Service at the bar was really good, there were multiple people that helped me during my meal. One thing is they were out of three of the beers I wanted right off the bat. Pretty cool vibe in the place and people just hanging with friends having drinks and food.
Came for Father's day brunch, and will definitely come back. great selection of vegetarian food.  Veggie Cuban and cheese grits were awesome. .and service was so good!
My favorite lunch spot in Ybor. Best greek salad of all time. Great srvice.

The Bricks gets a "1" in my book because they have terrible service.  Great food, but terrible service. 

I went there about 3pm on a Tuesday...which happened to be my birthday to have lunch with my mother.  Not only were we not greeted by the 3 staff standing around with NO other customers, but we were also not brought any menus or given direction about seating.  

We sat down and waited for a server to come by and ask for our drink order and bring menus.  No one ever did.  We got up and grabbed our own menus close to where the staff were standing.  They paid no attention.  After 3 or 4 more minutes we stood up to leave and they didn't care. So we walked out and I had my birthday lunch elsewhere. 

I  wrote to them on Facebook about our service and they promptly deleted my comment and ignored my message.  

I used to go to the Bricks all the time, but we've never been back since and I warn any new friends to not go there as well.

I walked into the restaraunt and the general scene was promising: a friendly environment with interesting decor like a diner, despite being poorly lit. I ordered the "King Fu pork bowl" and a macchiato, to which the waitress replied that their barista doesn't really make it the traditional way. I still ordered it. The macchiato came first, and to my surprise it was in a mug filled to the brim. I let the barista know that I ordered a macchiato, not a latte or cappuccino, and she said that she knows that, she made a macchiato. After a brief discussion I discovered she doesn't know what a macchiato was. I went back to my table. The food came. The pork was room temperature and the rice was plain. The dish lacked flavor overall. Maybe they don't specialize in rice bowls as it was a smaller item on their menu, but that was my experiance.
Friendly service & neat building. Depending on the atmosphere you are looking for, the music is a bit loud.

My friend and I visited Tampa for a concert, and about ten minutes away from the Atlanta airport he realized that he had purchased tickets for the wrong day. We had already made hotel reservations and bought the concert tickets, so he just had to pay same-day price for airfare: all in all about $800 more. "It was totally worth it," he later told me, "Because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life." All because we randomly picked the Bricks of Ybor from Yelp. I can't vouch for the peanut butter or meatless menu, but the meat sandwiches that we bought were absolutely phenomenal. I had the pulled pork, which was flavored with ponzu and served on Hawaiian sweet bread. It was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. We spent a few hours hanging out and drinking, during which time Brian, the owner, came out and talked to us, comped us a drink, let us try new appetizers he was developing (all for free) and generally made us feel really welcome. I kept my eyes open to the kind of crowd that came in and out of the restraunt. It seemed to draw everything from hipsters to geriatrics and strait-laced families with young kids. I think it speaks to both the diversity of the menu and the pleasant environment. We went back for drinks before and after the concert. It got very crowded but we still received excellant food, drinks and service. I give this restaurant my strongest recommendation, and it's the first place I'm going when I next visit Tampa.

I've always thought the idea of apple on a sandwich (that didn't involve peanut butter) as completely preposterous, because sweet things do not belong on sandwiches! So what did I order at The Bricks? Naturally, the Bird and Pig - which features chicken, bacon, apple, brie and agave nectar. It was definetly sweet. And savory. And absolutely, positively to die for. I loved every scrumptious bite of it.... except for the dry chicken breast. I'm not sure if it was just old, but either way it was dry and disappointing. Next on the menu was the deluxe grilled cheese sandwich, which was all sorts of yummy cheese, smothering delicious garden fresh basil (wow!), spinach and tomato. The first bite of this sandwich was knock-your-socks-off. The basil really stands out and it definitely warranted an audible moan. The next few bites weren't as spectacular, but I still loved the sandwich. I'd go with the Bird and Pig again if I had to choose. While we waited, we treated our faces to black bean dip (suggested by the waiter) and we enjoyed it. If you like black bean dip, then you'll like this one. We washed all of that down with a glass of liquid heroin, and all was right with the world. The end. Oh, and the service - spot on. The place is cute, the staff is attentive, and it's clear this place easily doubles as a comfy daytime spot and a lovely night spot - if that's your kinda thing.
Cute place, got there too late to eat,the drinks were good though, they have fresh ingredients and crushed ice!only bar in ybor I've seen with fresh things and a wide selection of booze

Food was delish. Stopped before a concert at The Ritz, it is just a block away and the perfect stop for reasonably priced fresh, healthy-ish meal before you wreck your liver. BFF had the Bird and Pig, she loved it. I had the Blackstar Bean Burger. It was spicy which in my opinion was perfect. The drinks are pricy, but well crafted. Our service was meh. A little slow, but we received the correct order and were informed of specials and what they were out of before we decided. I will totally be back next time I am in town.

Just came here for cocktails on a Tuesday night. The bar was full but not very busy otherwise. We got the huckle punch and Constantine. The huckleberry vodka in the huckle punch is one of my favorites so loved that drink and the Constantine also very good if you like bourbon! Service was very good and prices were reasonable. Had $3 taco deals and a very cute coffee bar so would definitely be interested in coming back to eat or for a good studying place!

Visited The Bricks this evening for dinner with a group of 6 and I think I can say we all enjoyed our experience  - I give it a solid 3-stars because I wasn't blown away by the food, ambiance or service but all were good if not a little above average. 

I started with an Old Fashioned which was sadly, quite watered down.  The table started with the Bricklayer Nachos which were good and a pretty decent size portion too.  For my dinner I had the Mediterranean Grilled Cheese - feta and mozzarella cheese, olive tapenade, baby spinach and portabello mushroom pressed in a piece of flatbread.  The first few bites were enjoyable but about a quarter of the way into it I realized how SALTY it was.  Unfortunately, it was a little one-note and better in concept than in execution in my opinion. 

Our waitress was pleasant and split the check 6-ways without us even having to ask, which I thought was really nice of her.  Atmosphere was unique but nothing worth coming back for.

Also, worth noting - The Bricks doesn't have its own parking lot so you'll have to find street parking (good luck), a paid parking lot lot or one of the local parking garages.

I had a good time at The Bricks of Ybor. The servise is really spot on and the quality of the food's pretty good. I had the pulled pork sandwich. It was pretty good. Nothing memorable but what makes this place a four star place are the happy hour beer prices and the interesting art inside. I loved the star wars art throughout this place and particularly loved the berpo and ern2d2 painting. Friendly, fun crowd that looks like they're coming to a John Waters costume party.

A good watering hole. Beer and coffee are decent!  Try UNITA REady Set Gose and UNITA summer ale.

Their bird & pig sandwich is the bomb. Brie cheese is one of my favs and this sandwich offers plenty. The Asian Slaw was a suggestion from our waitress and did not disappoint. It was yummy. The sesame seeds made all the difference. Full bar always has a variety of tasty drink options. This place is cool bc it has a vegan options for those folks with those dietary needs.

I walk in, and they're playing the greatest hits of De La Soul throughout lunch. They could have been serving Big Macs and that gets you four stars alone. 

I order a grilled cheese sandwich, and it comes with apple, plums, and bacon on some delicious bread with tortilla chips. And it is sublime. The cheese is perfectly melted, and the goodies inside are covered in wonderful gooey dairy greatness. 

I order a cafe con leche while getting some work done on my laptop. It is flawlessly prepared by a lovely server, and I'm a coffee snob. And if I didn't get buried in work stuff, I was jonesing for one of those half-price martinis they serve on Thursdays.

Wonderful atmosphere (the skatepark staff makes it friendly and fun), great food, delicious coffee, a full bar, and lots of different options. This place is a total home run, and a can't miss for anyone in Ybor.

The Bricks completely lives up to the hype. Don't leave without trying their amazing Basil-infused lemonade! Really chill cafe-like vibe, with a creative comfort food menu (peanut butter sandwiches!), and full table servic. In a few weeks they will be opening a quiet "study hall" space for laptop lurkers, making this a killer telecommute/study spot.

I'd been following the progress of The Bricks via their FB page for some time - I'm happy to report that the end product lives up to the expectations (exceeds them, even!). The first thing you notice is the atmosphere: laid-back & friendly, fostering a close-knit/ community feel that encourages you to slow down and linger for a bit longer, enjoying the company. When it comes to the menu, it's full of simple foods that have been completely mastered. I suggest the Peanut Butter Bar (choose your bread, peanut butter, and toppers). The Roasted Garlic Hummus is amazing, as is the Italian Brick sandwich. As far as coffee goes - they won't disappoint, I'm partial to the Brickaccino (frozen coffee). Another standout factor is their beer selection - which alone is worth strolling by for. All in all, The Bricks as a 5-Star stop, you won't soon forget.

If you have ever dreamed of owning a bad ass bar and restaurant, with phenomenal and creative food, solid service, and atmosphere as cool as - well as cool as the bricks in the streets of Ybor City - don't go here. It will be likely to depress you to see that your dream has already been done so well that there just isnt much improvement. 
Well, if there was parking, that would be an improvement - but that's about it. I work nearby and rock their little patio in the back about once a week, it just never disappoints. The CURE is my favorite sandwich but i dont think there are any bad items on the menu - not even the vegetarian ones, and you know how bad those CAN be!

If you are on the west end of Ybor, or staying at the hotels nearby, or just stepped off the streetcar and want to figure out what Ybor City has come to mean these days - the Bricks of Ybor should be your first stop!

My 2 favorite guy friends and I came here for Valentine's Day this year! I love everything about this place.  Every time I have visited there has been a friendly/diverse crowd and good music. I really like the atmosphere and the local artwork that is displayed throughout the restaurant. I highly recommend the brick layer nachos! My friends and I ate every bite and I honestly will most likely order that as my meal next time. The night we visited they had 50% off bottles of wine and after splitting the cost with one of my friends it was only $7 (need I say more?).  I ordered the brick layer salad with tuna for my meal. I ordered something lighter due to my massive nacho intake and the salad was good but it was similar to a house salad you can get anywhere. They have a very eclectic menu and next time I will probably try one of the many grilled cheese sandwiches listed on the menu. I will definitely be back!

A couple of nights ago the Tampa Bay Lady Bloggers met at The Bricks for our monthly book club meeting. The staff was very welcoming and was happy to push together several tables for us. Our server was so nice and helpful and cheerfully took a group photo for us (annoying bloggers). The "hole in the wall" atmosphere at The Bricks is fun and eclectic, with local art for sale lining the walls. I loved the laid-back, hip feeling of the place. I had the "brick,paper,scissors" martini and it was so refreshing and delicous that I had to get a second with my entree. The table shared an order of the "bricklayer" nachos and they were okay, but the house-made salsa on the side was out of this world. For my entree I got the "bird and pig", based on so many great Yelp recommendations. It did not disappoint with thick, crispy bacon, sweet apples and agave nectar, tasty chicken and delicious pressed "sweet" bread. I almost caved in and got the Ahi tuna BLT because it looked so good on the menu...I'll definitely be back and try that next time to compare. Thank you Bricks for hosting our meet-up. See you again soon I hope! My blog post about our meeting at The Bricks is here: http://carolinecalcote.com/2012/06/28/tampa-bay-lady-bloggers-book-club/
Terrible selection of food. No "real sweet tea" first and last time visit" anywhere that doesn't carry real sweet tea automatic gets a 1*

My wife and I have visited twice, and another time with friends. While we like the food and beer choices, the service is inexcusably very slow. We visited on a Saturday afternoon around 5:00 and the place was only 1/3 full. Took a while for our server to greet us, arrived just when we were about to get up and leave. Ordered a beer for each of us and waited at least 10 minutes before I finally got up to ask the bartender about our drinks (after watching him not making any drinks for several minutes and serving a few others who just arrived at the bar). I could barely get the words out before he says they'll be right up. I sit back down, and he still doesn't pour them. We were about to leave again when another bartender made eye contact and she poured the drinks and brought them to us. While our waitress was friendly, she should have been checking on our drinks. Same slow experience with the other two visits, this time we are certain we will not be back.

Based this visit entirely upon previous Yelp reviews, which as usual we're spot on. Great atmosphere and feel to this place - Kind of an art house meets coffee house meets Animal House environment. Very unusual. In a good way. The servise was relaxed, social and great. The beverages were delicious and the menu was quite interesting. I so wanted the food to be much better than it was. Tried the Bird and Pig, a specialty grilled cheese and a couple apps. Everything was good but not great. In truth, if I was judging on food alone, there would be three stars instead of four. But the atmosphere and the staff clearly deserved the extra star, and I'll head back to try some other items on the menu next visit.
My favorite lunch spot in Ybor. Best greek salad of all time. Great service.
My favorite lunch spot in Ybor. Best greek salad of all time. Great service.

Very fresh food- they actually make their own stuff! We ate lunch at the bar and the bartender went out of his way to help my husband find a good gluten free option. 

I ordered the black bean burger and it was delicious! Great atmosphere as well. Definitely recommend this place as there are not all that many fresh and relatively healthy places in the area. Wish we had found it sooner!
Really like the Bricks. Always a new experience when i go. The coffee, good. The cocktails, better! The ambiance is hip. The food is pretty good too.

I read the reviews on Yelp and decided to check out Bricks of Ybor for myself. 

Nice atmosphere and hip music playing in the background. I sat at the bar and watched the flat screen televisions (they were playing the History Channel on one TV. & "Shaun of the Dead" on another TV.). 

Good beer on tap (I tried the IPA -- it was good) and a small menu specializing in appetizers, salads & sandwiches. I ordered the hummus plate and the iceberg wedge salad -- both were delicious. The blue cheese dressing on the salad was particularly scrumptious. 

For one beer and an app and a salad, my bill came to just under $25 before tip -- kinda expensive (considering they no longer serve the "salmon spread" on the hummus plate -- should that really be priced at $10, still?).
I love this place. Everything I've had seems really fresh. The hummus is really tasty and the ambiance is nice and relaxed.

I am not nearly cool enough to go here. The waiter was not unfriendly, but he was much more friendly to some ladies who sat near me with full sleeves of tattoos. I ordered the black bean burger, it was so flavor less and thin it could have been omitted. The mayo on the sandwich and mixed greens on the side, along with the pickle, we're the best part of the meal. My beer was alright, but if I am going to spend $7 on a pint it should be delicious or high gravity, this was neither, and since no prices appeared next to the draft list, the price was a bit of a shock.

I had a good time at The Bricks of Ybor. The servise is really spot on and the quality of the food's pretty good. I had the pulled pork sandwich. It was pretty good. Nothing memorable but what makes this place a four star place are the happy hour beer prices and the interesting art inside. I loved the star wars art throughout this place and particularly loved the berpo and ern2d2 painting. Friendly, fun crowd that looks like they're coming to a John Waters costume party.

We cam here for my wife's birthday this year that also just so happens to be Cinco De Mayo. We didn't want to go to a mexican joint so we chose the Bricks after reading some specials that they had going online. I have to say it was a good night and a lot of fun. Good drinks as well as food. Great ambiance, this is an older building in Ybor that they really did a great job of restoring. These guys are always having great food and happy hour specials. You won't be disappointed.

The Bricks has a super cool vibe. I've visited multiple times for dinner and once for drinks. I'm always impressed with their sandwiches and other food. Normally everything is very fresh and tasty. They have a good sized line up of craft beers most of them local to the area, which is something I'm always looking for. 

It's sort of a dive-y location on the outskirts of the main part of Ybor. Late night they have a small menu of appetizers/small plates and have a DJ. It's clientele leads to some awesome people watching. 

All in all, definitely worth a try. It's not super fancy, so it's perfect for a casual dinner or a new place to try to grab a beer (there's a full bar as well).

This is where the cool kids hang and there's reasons for it. The beer and the food! Tons of vegetarian and even vegan options.
I'm not either but I do love that black bean burger and the salads are to die for.
The staff is great and always sweet and accommodating. 
The place is usually filled with great art and an eccentric lot of people. I gave this place five stars because I would be lying if I said I didn't love this place. It's my vibe.
It can be yours also.
Yup! Just referred to myself as a cool kid.:D

This place is listed as vegetarian-friendly and it is, provided that you eat eggs, cheese, and whatever else they put on the food without listing it in the menu description. Unfortunately this place was a nightmare for me as a vegan. I ordered the veggie cuban with no swiss or honey mustard since those were the only non-vegan ingredients listed in the description, and if it wasn't for the server mentioning "oh that's a great choice; the chef puts an egg on it too," then I would have gotten a sandwich with egg. After I stressed "no animal products, no egg, no dairy, no butter," the server responded with "oh well you know the egg isn't actually meat" as opposed to, you know, respecting my dietary restrictions.

I have no intention of returning, due to the lack of clarity on the menu and the server's rudeness when I was expressing my allergies/restrictions. Maybe if the restaurant lists all of the ingredients and trains their staff on how to not be rude to someone who was rightfully annoyed at almost getting an item I couldn't eat, then it might be worth a recommendation. But then again, it's not a vegan-friendly establishment despite it being vegetarian-friendly.

This was my first time here and I would recommend it! I had the Liquid Heroin (espresso, chocolate and milk) and the Bird and Pig. These two are the Bricks specialities. The Bird and Pig has chicken, bacon, apple, Brie, and honey. It is a perfect combination of salty and sweet. For dessert, we had the Ice Cream Sammy. A chocolate chip cookie with vanilla bean ice cream and chocolate syrup. I was a bit disappointed on the dessert because I was expecting the cookie to be soft and warm, it was the opposite; very hard. Overall the atmosphere is nice and I would come back to try some of the other specialties they have!

The husband and I had a kid free day so we decided to have a (gasp) lunch date.

 We picked The Bricks because...well why the hell not.  As soon as we walked in I loved the place.  It was bright and cozy at the same time.  The staff was super friendly and we got the vibe that we could hang out all day if we wanted.

I ordered the most delicious "adult" coffee to drop kick the sleepiness out of my head.  The coffee was SUPER yummy and the liquor did the trick.

It took me a while to figure out what I wanted to eat because everything on the menu looked soooo good and I was super hungry.  In the end, I decided on the Harvest Grill Cheese Sandwich.....nom nom noom.....I was not dissappointed.  It hit the spot and filled my belly with melty cheesy goodness.  The bread was fresh, crunchy, tender and tasty.  The sandwich innards were porportioned perfect.  The Gouda, bacon and apple playing off each other in perfect harmony.

GO HERE AND EAT!  I cannot wait to go again and feel this will be a staple on our lunch resturant list.  Even if your not hungry this would be a wonderful place to have a drink and just chill day or night.

Thanks Bricks for a great lunch!
fun place with a nice atmosphere. Ordered the Elvis which is a good sandwich with peanut butter honey bananana and bacon! it sounds weird but it was delicious.

The Bricks of Ybor is a restaurant, bar, and coffee bar in Ybor City and also has live music and special events at times. It is affiliated with the SkatePark of Tampa (SpoT) which has a shop next door and there are skateboard decks mounted on the walls of The Bricks as artwork and they play skate videos on the TVs above the bar; as I'm a skater myself, this is if anything just the icing on the cake for me. 

However, The Bricks' ardent support of skateboarding would not be enough to garner a five-star review alone, but thankfully it measures up in all other regards. The interior atmosphere is lively, inviting, and unique. The waitstaff and bartenders are on point, outgoing, friendly, and most importantly, quite prompt. As to the food, it's fairly simply fare but very tasty and very well-prepared. Tacos, a variety of Cuban sandwich variants, and some salads compose the lion's share of the menu. I had the Bird & Pig Cuban sandwich and also an order of chips and queso dip. The queso was especially good, which impressed me because too often things like queso are simply after-thoughts at bar-type restaurants. The sandwich itself was also very good. They have a full bar with a good selection of bourbons and ryes and also an expectedly good selection of beer, with an emphasis on Tampa's local brews. The wine list also looked better than you'd think for a casual bar atmosphere. Overall, it's clear they're investing in quality here. 

While their skateboarding association was enough to grab my attention to The Bricks, their stellar food and service are what really sets them apart. Ybor has a reputation for food being hit or miss, as is the case with many touristy areas, but The Bricks I found to be simply and casual yet truly impressive.

I love the Bricks! We live in Ybor and this is one of our favorite lunch spots. I always have a hard time selecting between two sandwiches - The Elvis which is a peanut butter, banana and bacon sandwich or the Bird and Pig - roasted chicken, bacon, brie, apple, pressed on a Hawaiian sweet roll. Bricks always offers weekly specials and featured drinks. The crowd is always fun and the staff is friendly.

nice place for gatherings and hanging out. Friendly staff. 

Food was OK. Not bad, not good, it just sat somewhere in the middle.

Seems like a good place ...very chill and low key..not my particular favorite food ( more on the healthy side) but still good quality food and service with a fun video game theme once a week ...good place to check out

Visited The Bricks this evening for dinner with a group of 6 and I think I can say we all enjoyed our experience  - I give it a solid 3-stars because I wasn't blown away by the food, ambiance or service but all were good if not a little above average. 

I started with an Old Fashioned which was sadly, quite watered down.  The table started with the Bricklayer Nachos which were good and a pretty decent size portion too.  For my dinner I had the Mediterranean Grilled Cheese - feta and mozzarella cheese, olive tapenade, baby spinach and portabello mushroom pressed in a piece of flatbread.  The first few bites were enjoyable but about a quarter of the way into it I realized how SALTY it was.  Unfortunately, it was a little one-note and better in concept than in execution in my opinion. 

Our waitress was pleasant and split the check 6-ways without us even having to ask, which I thought was really nice of her.  Atmosphere was unique but nothing worth coming back for.

Also, worth noting - The Bricks doesn't have its own parking lot so you'll have to find street parking (good luck), a paid parking lot lot or one of the local parking garages.

We walked into The Bricks of Ybor and were immediately greeted by the owner and taken on a tour. He showed us the studio area next door, the small patio in the back, and the food prep area. He also explained the menu and gave some recommendations. I've never been treated that way at a restaurant and it was an awesome touch. The food was great. The waitress did bring my husband the wrong sandwich but by the time we figured it out, it wasn't worth mentioning. He liked whatever it was she brought him. The beer selection was very good. The atmosphere is laid back and unique. They have games to play while you enjoy your drinks. The music is awesome. All in all, I love this place!

Came hungry and left full but not stuffed. The goodness wrap was named appropriately. Hummus with cucumber, tomato, lettuce, feta cheese and I added avocado was very flavorful. No need for any sauce of any kind. Had the potato salad as a side and though it was a bit bland, added a little salt to it, it was still good. Glad they don't add mayo to it and tasted home made for sure. Nice ambience too, decorated for Halloween. I'm not a fan of TV's while dining, but will always give a pass when they have good tunes playing so don't have to listen to TV. Only saw 2 servers on but it wasn't that busy on this Sunday afternoon. Server was knowledgeable and personable so not sure why others complained about rudeness. Saw none of that.
Great bar/café! Such a great place to hang, inside is beautiful and outside you can hear nice music while having a coffee and a cig! Definitely coming back! Loved it

I'm pretty sure telling a patron you are going to follow them into he women's restroom is some form of sexual harassment. I have NEVER been treated like that ever in an establishment. Hopefully, for the greater good of the restraunt, that manager is no longer there.

This might be my first five star rating. This place was absolutely awesome and I cannot wait until I go back for a second time. Our sever, Millie, was friendly and efficient from the moment we sat down. The atmosphere of the place was unique, and the food was among the most unique in Tampa that I have experienced in years. Wanted to try the pig and bird sammich but when I got there I decided on the Pacific Rim. The Asian slaw and bbq theme was too much to pass up. Pretty cool vibe in the place and people just hanging with friends having drinks and food.

It is definitely a place to bring your friends and chat. I love their different types of Peanut Butter sandwiches. Amazing! Not only that, but the inside environment is just so positive and provides inspiration.

My wife got the Athena chicken sandwich and that was just so-so, with the overwhelming taste of feta disguising the low-quality factory chicken they use for the sandwich. The best part of our collective meals was the mixed greens we ordered as a side, so I wouldn't exactly recommend ordering food here unless you're completely hammered and taste is not a priority.
