What an eclectic hipster joint, right in the heart of Ybor. The restraunt name alone fits the atmosphere perfectly. The menu options are unique, what might sound like it wouldn't mesh on the palette ends up making you want seconds and if drinking enough-- thirds. This is a great place to have a drink and a scrumptious sandwich on a Sunday. I had the bird and pig, perfect combination of savory and sweet.
Terrible selection of food. No "real sweet tea" first and last time visit" anywhere that doesn't carry real sweet tea automatic gets a 1*

Lots of vegetarian options. The service was pretty fast. The skateboard wall was nice (Calvin & Hobbes represent!). The sandwich I got was a bit lacking in the flavor department. Really didn't know what to eat since I went here at night just before a binge of dancing and drinking. Didn't really feel into the peanut butter at that point in time. Next time I'll try their peanut butter creations, but I'll probably go for brunch or a late lunch since it seems the menu is more designed for that and not any pre-gaming.

Where do i start with this place! I love that they have local art on the walls/ always doing art shows the staff that works there always rocking smiles talking to all the guess a all around good atmosphere vibe I tip my hat to the head chef (Chef Ben) The food is always on point and i like when the cooks yell "ORDER UP" hahaha I can wright a book about how awesome this place is KEEP UP THE GOOD WORK and SEE YOU SOON!

This is more of a drinking place than dinner. I didn't enjoy dining here at all, the service was slow and the acoustics of the place made It impossible to have a conversation. The veggie cubano was pretty good and the drinks were strong though.
Really like the Bricks. Always a new experience when i go. The coffee, good. The cocktails, better! The ambiance is hip. The food is pretty good too.
My favorite drinks place to imbibe before a show in Ybor. Kyle is spot on every time with what is seemingly the exact thing I want before I even know it. Also, the nachos. Trust me!

First of all I would like to say this is a pretty cool place. They have a great selection of beer and booze. The bartenders were very attentive and made awesome drinks. I was there on a Thursday night with a wedding party of about 12 people and we were having a great night. This is where I would love to end this review because based on the atmosphere and bartenders, this is a really chill place to hang out in ybor. Unfortunately, there is more to the story.

Later in the night, the bar started clearing out. The only people in the bar were myself, the wedding party I was with, the bartenders, and 3 other people. That's it. We (the wedding party) thought it would be fun to do the wobble and since the DJ was playing hip-hip anyway, we figured that it wouldn't be an issue to request that he play the wobble. After All, there wasn't many people in the bar anyway. Upon requesting to the DJ that we would like him to play the wobble he proceeded to respond with statements like "I refuse to play that song" "I don't like that song" "I'm not a jukebox". After briefly sharing our differences of opinion, I went to the bar to get a drink. At this time the DJ also walked up to the bar as we were kindly telling the bartender that they might want to reconsider their DJ choices because he was more concerned with what he wanted to hear, rather than what the patrons of the bar wanted to hear. Upon sharing our opinion with the bartender, the DJ butts in again to express that "I'm the DJ, and I'll play what I want to hear" that irritated me and I got a little heated. The bartender proceeded to cut me off because I argued with the DJ. I totally understand that, the bartender did the right thing there to calm down a situation. 

Point of my long story is, I really hope this place reconsiders their DJ choices in the future. They need someone that will play what the patrons want to hear and not what he wants to hear. Maybe that's just my opinion, but I feel that I make a strong case considering that by the time it was all said and done, our party was the only people in the bar. So, instead of 5 stars, I'm marking it a 3 based on the DJ alone.

Leaving this 2-star review in response to the food, not the place as a drinking/hangout spot...although the wine was crap, too. 2-Stars awarded for the Nintendo 64 and all of the nostalgia-worthy games, the decent choice of drafts (even if they were out of the draft I ordered), and the great service from the staff. The food, on the other hand, will make you wish you had eaten at home. My wife and I went out as a treat because we didn't feel like cooking, but the majority of our food was sub-par. I got the shrimp po-boy which was not a po-boy by definition (it was just shrimp on a crappy sandwich...no French bread, no Cajun sauce or even enough Cajun seasoning, and the shrimp was obviously frozen-thawed not fresh). One of the shrimps was even gray when I bit into it, and the sandwich itself smelled more like old fish than fresh shrimp. My wife got the Athena chicken sandwich and that was just so-so, with the overwhelming taste of feta disguising the low-quality factory chicken they use for the sandwich. The best part of our collective meals was the mixed greens we ordered as a side, so I wouldn't exactly recommend ordering food here unless you're completely hammered and taste is not a priority.

I ordered the bird and pig with Asian slaw.. $10. The sandwich is warm and pressed. It has pulled chicken inside. I was worried it would be dry. IT'S NOT. Very moist! Thick cut bacon and thinly sliced green apple.there was also a mayo type sauce. .tasted a bit sweet...Boy was this sandwich great!! The Asian slaw was delicately dressed with the careful handed use of sesame oil. Fantastic! And they have a large assortment of Florida brewed beers. The Wynwood iPA was so flavorful and foam on top just pillowy. Atmosphere relaxed. Staff is friendly and servic great. I was here on a Thursday night about 6pm. Nice and clean.

Yummy food, good vibes, & nice service. Music wasn't too loud. Could hold a conversation without hearing everyone else's. I had the Bird & Pig (the way it comes) with the Mac & Cheese. I also had the Hukilau. Not a fan. It sounded sweeter than it was. Still giving it a 4 for the food srvice and atmosphere. It's not their fault I didn't like the alcohol. Had a quick bite of the nachos and may have to orders those for the table next visit.

For days I have tried to put a side the terrible experience I had, I really don't like to put a bad review, but most of all I deeply appreciate when businesses treat everyone with respect and priority, and for some reason and actually for no reason.
I walked in and noticed I have to go to the bar for service, there were no available seats, so I stood at the beginning of the bar from the entrance, made an eye contact with the bar tender, 5 min passed he still didn't come to me so I looked over for a menu and grabbed it myself, shortly after he reached to me and took my order of drinks and food... 10 min passed and he didn't prepare my drinks, he left the bar area, and another guy came to replace him, he asked us if we needed help, I told him we already ordered, mean while I'm waiting and waiting and I see our server went to take out food for people, totally forgot about us, he could have at least tell the other two guys who were at the bar ( one of them was the owner) to make us the drink...
Then the owner came to me and he told me I should have told the guy that replaced him to make me the drinks, i told him how could I know it works that way?
And instead of trying to make excuses for why I don't have my drinks and blaming me for it, he obviously didn't care for what u had to say but I tried explain him how long I've been waiting and that I should have been taken care off and that he's been very rude for trying to excuse the situation instead of handling It property...
End of story, He got mad he said I'm the owner and that I'm not going to talk to him that way and he walked away from me!


So to sum it all up, I waited a while until I was served, the tender argued with me that chocolate always has milk inside ( just a lack of knowledge) the owner saw us waiting and waiting , looked at us while serving others, and than he got the nerve to be mad at me for being upset....!!!!
Bird and Pig and the Tuna BLT are awesome!  Delicious cold beer. Thanks for the recommendation, Yelp!
Bird and Pig and the Tuna BLT are awesome!  Delicious cold beer. Thanks for the recommendation, Yelp!

We went at a slow time on a weekday afternoon for a late lunch because we were all wanting sandwiches. So between us all we had: the Bird & Pig, BBQ quesadilla, ahi BLT, clubhouse and kids pbj. All the sandwiches were great! Service was a bit slow though. If I was in the area again I may try again but I would not go out of my way to eat here.

This is THE BEST spot for food and drinks in Ybor.  The drinks are amazing and the food is top notch. Cool, laid back atmosphere and amazing bar!! All of the staff are helpful and accommodating!! Best happy hour!!!

Full disclosure: My experience might just have been an isolated, rare occurrence. I arrived to The Brick and sat myself at the bar. After 15 minutes of zero service I was getting ready to leave but I noticed the waiting staff on the main floor looked active and on top of things. I decided to transition from the lack of service bar to the main floor and, literally, as soon as I sat down I had a waiter hand me a menu, take my drink order and before even a blink I had a Bloody Mary in front on me. Moral of this story, careful sitting at the bar since the service there seemed to be lacking. I'm sure it was the timing since my overall experience was a thumbs up. 

I ordered the loaded Bloody Mary. The drink was simple but very delightful, clearly proving that less is more. The drink had a little satisfying kick that's normal to any Bloody Mary. Overall- very satisfied with their Bloody Mary, so much in fact I ordered two. Maybe a little more body to it but not a must. 

Food: I ordered the Tuna BLT with the side of Asian slaw. Overall: GREAT. The theme here is clearly simple. They exploit every taste which is gratifying since that's the most important thing. The slaw was crisp and surprisingly very refreshing. Now, the tuna can only be described as crafted by a masterful craftsman! Yes, I said it. It tasted better than it looked and that's hard todo since it looked as if out of a magazine. Nothing but quality dining. 

I place four starts because of the first part of my experience but other than that it was a good experience and I I'll come to The Brick again.

The Bricks is a hipster haven, but don't let that deter you if you don't wear non-prescription glasses and flannel. I'm always the least cool person in here and no one seems to mind. (Although maybe I AM cool -- last time I was here the DJ was playing Hall & Oates most likely to be ironic, but I  genuinely enjoyed it.)

The menu is mostly sandwiches and some salads. It's all about the Bird & Pig sandwich. I have a hard time straying from this delicacy of chicken, bacon, brie, and apples on pressed sweet bread. Sweet, check. Salty, check. Crunchy, check. 

Nice selection of local and craft brews, too.

I like some of the cocktails here but the food is mediocre. Ive never understood why it gets the ratings on food that it does, but then again we are in Tampa. Its basically like food you could whip up in a few minutes at home using your microwave for a 3rd of the cost. Except not as tasty. Anyone who loves eating here has the palate of a 14-year-old boy. Maybe its time they get an actual kitchen.

We walked into The Bricks of Ybor and were immediately greeted by the owner and taken on a tour. He showed us the studio area next door, the small patio in the back, and the food prep area. He also explained the menu and gave some recommendations. I've never been treated that way at a restaurant and it was an awesome touch. The food was great. The waitress did bring my husband the wrong sandwich but by the time we figured it out, it wasn't worth mentioning. He liked whatever it was she brought him. The beer selection was very good. The atmosphere is laid back and unique. They have games to play while you enjoy your drinks. The music is awesome. All in all, I love this place!

While I was in Tampa for the last 2 years, The Bricks was a second home. Great food and even greater people. I moved back to Seattle and left making friends. Wish I could've brought The Bricks and my new friends back with me. Definitely a place for locals and visitors to check out!

It was so difficult deciding what to order here. I was in the mood for a skanky chai latte, but the skinny bitch latte just had that calorie conscious ring to it.

After a bit of thought I decided, skanky it shall be!

This has got to be one of my favorite places in Tampa. I had never really put a pulse on "hipster" in Tampa, but I found the closest thing to it at Bricks. Plenty of space to lounge here with a nice offering that ranged from caffeinated beverages to brews and snacks.

I would have never typically thought to throw bacon on a peanut butter and banana sandwich and then drizzle with honey, but I'm glad someone did.
The Elvis sandwich is a hunka, hunka, burning yum!

I would give this place five stars all day, except for the fact that service is slow. Like, dial-up slow. Like larvae to butterfly metamorphosis slow. So slow in fact that on a pretty *slow* afternoon, it would take 20 minutes just to get an iced chai even though you have a clear view of queue and activity of the servers. So slow that from time of check request to actually receiving it, was about another 20 minutes.

While the laid back atmosphere is one of the things that makes this place so cool, it's also the incredibly laid back service that could put a damper on things if you're in a rush.

Have come to The Bricks a few times as I wait for classes, there is wifi and it's a nice environment to sit, eat, grab a beer and do some homework. If I'm in Ybor for an extended period of time and have to wait, I usually try to make it here as much as I can.

This was my first time here and I would recommend it! I had the Liquid Heroin (espresso, chocolate and milk) and the Bird and Pig. These two are the Bricks specialities. The Bird and Pig has chicken, bacon, apple, Brie, and honey. It is a perfect combination of salty and sweet. For dessert, we had the Ice Cream Sammy. A chocolate chip cookie with vanilla bean ice cream and chocolate syrup. I was a bit disappointed on the dessert because I was expecting the cookie to be soft and warm, it was the opposite; very hard. Overall the atmosphere is nice and I would come back to try some of the other specialties they have!

I read the reviews on Yelp and decided to check out Bricks of Ybor for myself. 

Nice atmosphere and hip music playing in the background. I sat at the bar and watched the flat screen televisions (they were playing the History Channel on one TV. & "Shaun of the Dead" on another TV.). 

Good beer on tap (I tried the IPA -- it was good) and a small menu specializing in appetizers, salads & sandwiches. I ordered the hummus plate and the iceberg wedge salad -- both were delicious. The blue cheese dressing on the salad was particularly scrumptious. 

For one beer and an app and a salad, my bill came to just under $25 before tip -- kinda expensive (considering they no longer serve the "salmon spread" on the hummus plate -- should that really be priced at $10, still?).
It's a beer pub so don't go to eat a meal. Beer was great but not all of them were available at the time I visited [April] so....??

Since moving to Tampa about three weeks ago, I have found some ridiculously good restaurants thanks to Yelp and friends' recommendations. 

The Bricks has been on my list of places to try for a while now, and I finally made it last night. 

My friend & I walked in and were greeted immediately by the staff who told us to sit where we wanted. The place was fairly empty on a Tuesday at 7pm. I've heard it's packed on weekends, so perhaps going on off-nights is key. 

We started off with the Bricklayer, a fancy name for extra delicious nachos that are topped with queso, avocado cream, olives, and jalapeños. The salsa that comes on the side is awesome - super fresh, flavorful, and not too watery. This is a big appetizer and probably a bit too much for two girls before dinner. If I ordered it again, it would be as a bar snack rather than an app. 

For dinner, I had to try the Bird & the Pig. Wow - that pressed sweet bread combined with the salty bacon and chicken, paired with crisp apples and agave nectar? Yeah, the distinct flavors come together nicely to create one hell of a sandwich. 

I tasted my friend's black bean burger and liked that, too. 

The only thing I tasted that didn't blow me away was the roasted potato salad I got on the side. I'll probably just go with the mixed greens salad next time. 

Aside from the food, the environment is cool, too. I really liked all the local artists' work adorning the walls. 

There is ample parking nearby, including a garage on 15th that only charges $1 for the first 3 hours.

Just came here for cocktails on a Tuesday night. The bar was full but not very busy otherwise. We got the huckle punch and Constantine. The huckleberry vodka in the huckle punch is one of my favorites so loved that drink and the Constantine also very good if you like bourbon! Service was very good and prices were reasonable. Had $3 taco deals and a very cute coffee bar so would definitely be interested in coming back to eat or for a good studying place!

A must when you are in Ybor.  I ate and drank here multiple times a day for my 5 day trip to Tampa.  Every single meal was spectacular.  The Skinny bitch latte is perfect to start the day.  The proper grilled cheese is amazing, just wish they would have tomato soup to go along with it.  And you can't find better bartenders anywhere else in town.

Where do I start:
Phenomenal food
Excellent Bartender - I didn't know what to drink and bartender created one to her liking
Great Atmosphere
Great music - DJ on Friday Night was awesome
Even the free water in the beginning tasted amazingly
Definitely would go again
Great craft beers, friendly bartenders, and AMAZING, delishous food. The vegetarian Cuban sandwich was wonderful!

I walked into the restaurant and the general scene was promising: a friendly environment with interesting decor like a diner, despite being poorly lit.

I ordered the "King Fu pork bowl" and a macchiato, to which the waitress replied that their barista doesn't really make it the traditional way. I still ordered it.

The macchiato came first, and to my surprise it was in a mug filled to the brim. I let the barista know that I ordered a macchiato, not a latte or cappuccino, and she said that she knows that, she made a macchiato. After a brief discussion I discovered she doesn't know what a macchiato was. I went back to my table. 

The food came. The pork was room temperature and the rice was plain. The dish lacked flavor overall. 

Maybe they don't specialize in rice bowls as it was a smaller item on their menu, but that was my experience.

It is definitely a place to bring your friends and chat. I love their different types of Peanut Butter sandwiches. Amazing! Not only that, but the inside environment is just so positive and provides inspiration.

A must when you are in Ybor.  I ate and drank here multiple times a day for my 5 day trip to Tampa.  Every single meal was spectacular.  The Skinny bitch latte is perfect to start the day.  The proper grilled cheese is amazing, just wish they would have tomato soup to go along with it.  And you can't find better bartenders anywhere else in town.

The Bricks has a super cool vibe. I've visited multiple times for dinner and once for drinks. I'm always impressed with their sandwiches and other food. Normally everything is very fresh and tasty. They have a good sized line up of craft beers most of them local to the area, which is something I'm always looking for. 

It's sort of a dive-y location on the outskirts of the main part of Ybor. Late night they have a small menu of appetizers/small plates and have a DJ. It's clientele leads to some awesome people watching. 

All in all, definitely worth a try. It's not super fancy, so it's perfect for a casual dinner or a new place to try to grab a beer (there's a full bar as well).

fun place with a nice atmosphere. Ordered the Elvis which is a good sandwich with peanut butter honey bananana and bacon! it sounds weird but it was delicious.

My friend and I visited Tampa for a concert, and about ten minutes away from the Atlanta airport he realized that he had purchased tickets for the wrong day. We had already made hotel reservations and bought the concert tickets, so he just had to pay same-day price for airfare: all in all about $800 more. "It was totally worth it," he later told me, "Because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life."

All because we randomly picked the Bricks of Ybor from Yelp. I can't vouch for the peanut butter or meatless menu, but the meat sandwiches that we bought were absolutely phenomenal. I had the pulled pork, which was flavored with ponzu and served on Hawaiian sweet bread. It was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. We spent a few hours hanging out and drinking, during which time Brian, the owner, came out and talked to us, comped us a drink, let us try new appetizers he was developing (all for free) and generally made us feel really welcome. 

I kept my eyes open to the kind of crowd that came in and out of the restaurant. It seemed to draw everything from hipsters to geriatrics and strait-laced families with young kids. I think it speaks to both the diversity of the menu and the pleasant environment. We went back for drinks before and after the concert. It got very crowded but we still received excellent food, drinks and service. I give this restaurant my strongest recommendation, and it's the first place I'm going when I next visit Tampa.

This is THE BEST spot for food and drinks in Ybor.  The drinks are amazing and the food is top notch. Cool, laid back atmosphere and amazing bar!! All of the staff are helpful and accommodating!! Best happy hour!!!

Very fresh food- they actually make their own stuff! We ate lunch at the bar and the bartender went out of his way to help my husband find a good gluten free option. 

I ordered the black bean burger and it was delicious! Great atmosphere as well. Definitely recommend this place as there are not all that many fresh and relatively healthy places in the area. Wish we had found it sooner!
It sucks, don't go!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Cold food, stuck up waiters, expensive drinks

I thoroughly enjoy going to the Bricks.  It's unique atmosphere with cheap, but tasty, food options combine for a great experience.  

The term hipster is thrown around a lot these days and while you may be greeted and surrounded by people in skinny jeans, wearing Toms shoes, IMAX glasses, and an extra piercing, you are treated no differently.  I always feel warmly welcomed and entertained.  

As it does have a large bar, it may get rowdy in the evenings, but the Bricks maintains a family-friendly atmosphere.  

I ate the Bird and Pig meal once, very very good, and the breakfast bagel the next time.  The fiancee had black bean soup and a grilled cheese sandwich.  Very tasty combination. 

Highly recommend!

We went at a slow time on a weekday afternoon for a late lunch because we were all wanting sandwiches. So between us all we had: the Bird & Pig, BBQ quesadilla, ahi BLT, clubhouse and kids pbj. All the sandwiches were great! Service was a bit slow though. If I was in the area again I may try again but I would not go out of my way to eat here.

The Bricks of Ybor is a restaurant, bar, and coffee bar in Ybor City and also has live music and special events at times. It is affiliated with the SkatePark of Tampa (SpoT) which has a shop next door and there are skateboard decks mounted on the walls of The Bricks as artwork and they play skate videos on the TVs above the bar; as I'm a skater myself, this is if anything just the icing on the cake for me. 

However, The Bricks' ardent support of skateboarding would not be enough to garner a five-star review alone, but thankfully it measures up in all other regards. The interior atmosphere is lively, inviting, and unique. The waitstaff and bartenders are on point, outgoing, friendly, and most importantly, quite prompt. As to the food, it's fairly simply fare but very tasty and very well-prepared. Tacos, a variety of Cuban sandwich variants, and some salads compose the lion's share of the menu. I had the Bird & Pig Cuban sandwich and also an order of chips and queso dip. The queso was especially good, which impressed me because too often things like queso are simply after-thoughts at bar-type restaurants. The sandwich itself was also very good. They have a full bar with a good selection of bourbons and ryes and also an expectedly good selection of beer, with an emphasis on Tampa's local brews. The wine list also looked better than you'd think for a casual bar atmosphere. Overall, it's clear they're investing in quality here. 

While their skateboarding association was enough to grab my attention to The Bricks, their stellar food and service are what really sets them apart. Ybor has a reputation for food being hit or miss, as is the case with many touristy areas, but The Bricks I found to be simply and casual yet truly impressive.

This was my first time here and I would recommend it! I had the Liquid Heroin (espresso, chocolate and milk) and the Bird and Pig. These two are the Bricks specialities. The Bird and Pig has chicken, bacon, apple, Brie, and honey. It is a perfect combination of salty and sweet. For dessert, we had the Ice Cream Sammy. A chocolate chip cookie with vanilla bean ice cream and chocolate syrup. I was a bit disappointed on the dessert because I was expecting the cookie to be soft and warm, it was the opposite; very hard. Overall the atmosphere is nice and I would come back to try some of the other specialties they have!

We cam here for my wife's birthday this year that also just so happens to be Cinco De Mayo. We didn't want to go to a mexican joint so we chose the Bricks after reading some specials that they had going online. I have to say it was a good night and a lot of fun. Good drinks as well as food. Great ambiance, this is an older building in Ybor that they really did a great job of restoring. These guys are always having great food and happy hour specials. You won't be disappointed.

Have come to The Bricks a few times as I wait for classes, there is wifi and it's a nice environment to sit, eat, grab a beer and do some homework. If I'm in Ybor for an extended period of time and have to wait, I usually try to make it here as much as I can.

My wife and I have visited twice, and another time with friends. While we like the food and beer choices, the servic is inexcusably very slow. We visited on a Saturday afternoon around 5:00 and the place was only 1/3 full. Took a while for our server to greet us, arrived just when we were about to get up and leave. Ordered a beer for each of us and waited at least 10 minutes before I finally got up to ask the bartender about our drinks (after watching him not making any drinks for several minutes and serving a few others who just arrived at the bar). I could barely get the words out before he says they'll be right up. I sit back down, and he still doesn't pour them. We were about to leave again when another bartender made eye contact and she poured the drinks and brought them to us. While our waitress was friendly, she should have been checking on our drinks. Same slow expereince with the other two visits, this time we are certain we will not be back.

Came hungry and left full but not stuffed. The goodness wrap was named appropriately. Hummus with cucumber, tomato, lettuce, feta cheese and I added avocado was very flavorful. No need for any sauce of any kind. Had the potato salad as a side and though it was a bit bland, added a little salt to it, it was still good. Glad they don't add mayo to it and tasted home made for sure. Nice ambience too, decorated for Halloween. I'm not a fan of TV's while dining, but will always give a pass when they have good tunes playing so don't have to listen to TV. Only saw 2 servers on but it wasn't that busy on this Sunday afternoon. Server was knowledgeable and personable so not sure why others complained about rudeness. Saw none of that.

I dined here for the first time with my daughter, who is a regular. We had the Hummus appetizer. I had the Bricks Club and she had the specialty Grilled Cheese. The food was fresh, tasty and full of flavor. The service was very good. The bottle of ice water they bring is a classy touch. The ambiance is eclectic. My daughter told me normally the place is full of hipsters, but the crowd was spare on the day we were there. The prices are reasonable and in line with the usual and customary norms for Tampa. I don't drink, but it looked like they have quite an assortment of craft beer available.

Great atmosphere, always a good variety of music playing, excellent food and an increasingly diverse drink menu make this possibly my favorite place in Tampa. The Bird and Pig could quite possibly be the best sandwich in the history of sandwiches! Chicken, bacon, Brie, agave on Hawaiian sweet bread....yum! Also, try Root Down on the drink menu. Tastes exactly like Root Beer!

A couple of nights ago the Tampa Bay Lady Bloggers met at The Bricks for our monthly book club meeting. The staff was very welcoming and was happy to push together several tables for us. Our server was so nice and helpful and cheerfully took a group photo for us (annoying bloggers). The "hole in the wall" atmosphere at The Bricks is fun and eclectic, with local art for sale lining the walls. I loved the laid-back, hip feeling of the place. I had the "brick,paper,scissors" martini and it was so refreshing and delicous that I had to get a second with my entree. The table shared an order of the "bricklayer" nachos and they were okay, but the house-made salsa on the side was out of this world. For my entree I got the "bird and pig", based on so many great Yelp recommendations. It did not disappoint with thick, crispy bacon, sweet apples and agave nectar, tasty chicken and delishous pressed "sweet" bread. I almost caved in and got the Ahi tuna BLT because it looked so good on the menu...I'll definately be back and try that next time to compare. Thank you Bricks for hosting our meet-up. See you again soon I hope! My blog post about our meeting at The Bricks is here: http://carolinecalcote.com/2012/06/28/tampa-bay-lady-bloggers-book-club/

Very fresh food- they actually make their own stuff! We ate lunch at the bar and the bartender went out of his way to help my husband find a good gluten free option. I ordered the black bean burger and it was delicious! Great atmosphere as well. Definitely recommend this place as there are not all that many fresh and relatively healthy places in the area. Wish we had found it sooner!

This is more of a drinking place than dinner. I didn't enjoy dining here at all, the service was slow and the acoustics of the place made It impossible to have a conversation. The veggie cubano was pretty good and the drinks were strong though.

I ordered the bird and pig with Asian slaw.. $10. The sandwich is warm and pressed. It has pulled chicken inside. I was worried it would be dry. IT'S NOT. Very moist! Thick cut bacon and thinly sliced green apple.there was also a mayo type sauce. .tasted a bit sweet...Boy was this sandwich great!! The Asian slaw was delicately dressed with the careful handed use of sesame oil. Fantastic! And they have a large assortment of Florida brewed beers. The Wynwood iPA was so flavorful and foam on top just pillowy. Atmosphere relaxed. Staff is friendly and servise great. I was here on a Thursday night about 6pm. Nice and clean.
Friendly service & neat building. Depending on the atmosphere you are looking for, the music is a bit loud.

Tasty place to grab a unique sandwich or something else with some tasty beer. I love the decor in this restaurant, as it seems to marry bricks, random tomfoolery, and nerdiness quite well. I've enjoyed most things there. The Bird and Pig was quite good as well as their veggie burger. They also have lots of theme nights, but I've never been to one.

While I was in Tampa for the last 2 years, The Bricks was a second home. Great food and even greater people. I moved back to Seattle and left making friends. Wish I could've brought The Bricks and my new friends back with me. Definitely a place for locals and visitors to check out!

The husband and I had a kid free day so we decided to have a (gasp) lunch date. We picked The Bricks because...well why the hell not. As soon as we walked in I loved the place. It was bright and cozy at the same time. The staff was super friendly and we got the vibe that we could hang out all day if we wanted. I ordered the most deliciuos "adult" coffee to drop kick the sleepiness out of my head. The coffee was SUPER yummy and the liquor did the trick. It took me a while to figure out what I wanted to eat because everything on the menu looked soooo good and I was super hungry. In the end, I decided on the Harvest Grill Cheese Sandwich.....nom nom noom.....I was not dissappointed. It hit the spot and filled my belly with melty cheesy goodness. The bread was fresh, crunchy, tender and tasty. The sandwich innards were porportioned perfect. The Gouda, bacon and apple playing off each other in perfect harmony. GO HERE AND EAT! I cannot wait to go again and feel this will be a staple on our lunch resturant list. Even if your not hungry this would be a wonderful place to have a drink and just chill day or night. Thanks Bricks for a great lunch!

Either ate or had drinks here a few times over the summer as my office was just upstairs.  I'm not a vegetarian, but the Goodness wrap is a knockout.  I also greatly enjoyed the chili I had here, though it was a special so I'm not sure how often it comes around.  I'm not really into the hipster vibe of the staff, but I never had any service problems and that's what is most important.  

I definitely don't live or die by The Bricks but it's a place I would suggest if you're ever in Ybor City.

They have a super friendly staff and a simple modern decor.

I enjoyed the Six Degrees of Kevin Bacon exhibit on display.

I got a really young and hip vibe from this place, and the sandwiches are amazing!

I have to say that the food here is good; however, the staff/service could be better. My sister and I came here for lunch and a few drinks. My sister ordered a drink off the menu and 10+min later, as we're finishing our lunch, the waitress comes back and says "sorry, our bartender doesn't know how to make that" ..... So the bartender doesn't know how to make the drinks listed on the menu? And the 10+mins. it took to tell us that, it could have ben googled and made. I don't want to bash this establishment, but the customer service has always been an issue here. I would recommend continued training to both current and new staffers to improve their level of knowledge and customer service

Leaving this 2-star review in response to the food, not the place as a drinking/hangout spot...although the wine was crap, too. 2-Stars awarded for the Nintendo 64 and all of the nostalgia-worthy games, the decent choice of drafts (even if they were out of the draft I ordered), and the great service from the staff. The food, on the other hand, will make you wish you had eaten at home. My wife and I went out as a treat because we didn't feel like cooking, but the majority of our food was sub-par. I got the shrimp po-boy which was not a po-boy by definition (it was just shrimp on a crappy sandwich...no French bread, no Cajun sauce or even enough Cajun seasoning, and the shrimp was obviously frozen-thawed not fresh). One of the shrimps was even gray when I bit into it, and the sandwich itself smelled more like old fish than fresh shrimp. My wife got the Athena chicken sandwich and that was just so-so, with the overwhelming taste of feta disguising the low-quality factory chicken they use for the sandwich. The best part of our collective meals was the mixed greens we ordered as a side, so I wouldn't exactly recommend ordering food here unless you're completely hammered and taste is not a priority.

I read the reviews on Yelp and decided to check out Bricks of Ybor for myself. 

Nice atmosphere and hip music playing in the background. I sat at the bar and watched the flat screen televisions (they were playing the History Channel on one TV. & "Shaun of the Dead" on another TV.). 

Good beer on tap (I tried the IPA -- it was good) and a small menu specializing in appetizers, salads & sandwiches. I ordered the hummus plate and the iceberg wedge salad -- both were delicious. The blue cheese dressing on the salad was particularly scrumptious. 

For one beer and an app and a salad, my bill came to just under $25 before tip -- kinda expensive (considering they no longer serve the "salmon spread" on the hummus plate -- should that really be priced at $10, still?).

If you're immune to salmonella poisoning then this is the perfect place for you! Very overpriced, minimum effort in providing authentic food NOT out of a can. They undercook the chicken and it taste like refrigerator. Please don't waste your hard earned cash on half assed food. Unless you just want drinks and a good time with friends, don't come here.

I thoroughly enjoy going to the Bricks.  It's unique atmosphere with cheap, but tasty, food options combine for a great experience.  

The term hipster is thrown around a lot these days and while you may be greeted and surrounded by people in skinny jeans, wearing Toms shoes, IMAX glasses, and an extra piercing, you are treated no differently.  I always feel warmly welcomed and entertained.  

As it does have a large bar, it may get rowdy in the evenings, but the Bricks maintains a family-friendly atmosphere.  

I ate the Bird and Pig meal once, very very good, and the breakfast bagel the next time.  The fiancee had black bean soup and a grilled cheese sandwich.  Very tasty combination. 

Highly recommend!

First of all I would like to say this is a pretty cool place. They have a great selection of beer and booze. The bartenders were very attentive and made awesome drinks. I was there on a Thursday night with a wedding party of about 12 people and we were having a great night. This is where I would love to end this review because based on the atmosphere and bartenders, this is a really chill place to hang out in ybor. Unfortunately, there is more to the story.

Later in the night, the bar started clearing out. The only people in the bar were myself, the wedding party I was with, the bartenders, and 3 other people. That's it. We (the wedding party) thought it would be fun to do the wobble and since the DJ was playing hip-hip anyway, we figured that it wouldn't be an issue to request that he play the wobble. After All, there wasn't many people in the bar anyway. Upon requesting to the DJ that we would like him to play the wobble he proceeded to respond with statements like "I refuse to play that song" "I don't like that song" "I'm not a jukebox". After briefly sharing our differences of opinion, I went to the bar to get a drink. At this time the DJ also walked up to the bar as we were kindly telling the bartender that they might want to reconsider their DJ choices because he was more concerned with what he wanted to hear, rather than what the patrons of the bar wanted to hear. Upon sharing our opinion with the bartender, the DJ butts in again to express that "I'm the DJ, and I'll play what I want to hear" that irritated me and I got a little heated. The bartender proceeded to cut me off because I argued with the DJ. I totally understand that, the bartender did the right thing there to calm down a situation. 

Point of my long story is, I really hope this place reconsiders their DJ choices in the future. They need someone that will play what the patrons want to hear and not what he wants to hear. Maybe that's just my opinion, but I feel that I make a strong case considering that by the time it was all said and done, our party was the only people in the bar. So, instead of 5 stars, I'm marking it a 3 based on the DJ alone.

I will certainly be coming by for a sammich at this place.

My favorite lunch spot in Ybor. Best greek salad of all time. Great service.

Lots of vegetarian options. The service was pretty fast. The skateboard wall was nice (Calvin & Hobbes represent!). The sandwich I got was a bit lacking in the flavor department. Really didn't know what to eat since I went here at night just before a binge of dancing and drinking. Didn't really feel into the peanut butter at that point in time. Next time I'll try their peanut butter creations, but I'll probably go for brunch or a late lunch since it seems the menu is more designed for that and not any pre-gaming.
It sucks, don't go!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Cold food, stuck up waiters, expensive drinks

I definately don't live or die by The Bricks but it's a place I would suggest if you're ever in Ybor City.

The Bricks has a super cool vibe. I've visited multiple times for dinner and once for drinks. I'm always impressed with their sandwiches and other food. Normally everything is very fresh and tasty. They have a good sized line up of craft beers most of them local to the area, which is something I'm always looking for. 

It's sort of a dive-y location on the outskirts of the main part of Ybor. Late night they have a small menu of appetizers/small plates and have a DJ. It's clientele leads to some awesome people watching. 

All in all, definitely worth a try. It's not super fancy, so it's perfect for a casual dinner or a new place to try to grab a beer (there's a full bar as well).

I found myself enjoying the overall experience and reluctant to leave.  A good value at less than $10.

Great, laid-back atmosphere, terrific food. The ahi was good quality, as were the hummus and curry dip. We're going back for the peanut butter sandwiches.

2 words THE CURE! I ended up here after a night of one too many drinks (it happens). A friend recommended this place for a hang over cure! She was not mistaken! After reviewing their menu, which seemed a bit obnoxious, (I'm talking quirky names that require you read the description to be able to decipher what you're eating) I settled on the sandwich with an egg on it! Im a sucker for a runny egg on just about anything! Messy eggs, bacon, mozzarella, jalapeño aioli, on toasted cuban bread; this holy grail of a sandwich is called THE CURE! I have been back a few times to this establishment just for this sandwich, the mimosas too. Oh yea they have liquor so you can totally have drinks here. 

The ambience is very chill. There are a good amount of tables inside and bar seating; no outside seating. I have been here on a Sunday for brunch and found it to be pretty family/kid friendly. The whole place and most of the staff is painfully hipster but it works. The bathrooms are clean and there is a small back patio with mural art.

Have come to The Bricks a few times as I wait for classes, there is wifi and it's a nice environment to sit, eat, grab a beer and do some homework. If I'm in Ybor for an extended period of time and have to wait, I usually try to make it here as much as I can.

Based this visit entirely upon previous Yelp reviews, which as usual we're spot on. Great atmosphere and feel to this place - Kind of an art house meets coffee house meets Animal House environment. Very unusual. In a good way. The service was relaxed, social and great. The beverages were delicious and the menu was quite interesting. 
I so wanted the food to be much better than it was. Tried the Bird and Pig, a specialty grilled cheese and a couple apps. Everything was good but not great. In truth, if I was judging on food alone, there would be three stars instead of four. But the atmosphere and the staff clearly deserved the extra star, and I'll head back to try some other items on the menu next visit.

I've always thought the idea of apple on a sandwich (that didn't involve peanut butter) as completely preposterous, because sweet things do not belong on sandwiches!  

So what did I order at The Bricks?  Naturally, the Bird and Pig - which features chicken, bacon, apple, brie and agave nectar.   It was definitely sweet.  And savory.  And absolutely, positively to die for.  I loved every scrumptious bite of it.... except for the dry chicken breast.  I'm not sure if it was just old, but either way it was dry and disappointing.

Next on the menu was the deluxe grilled cheese sandwich, which was all sorts of yummy cheese, smothering delicious garden fresh basil (wow!), spinach and tomato.   The first bite of this sandwich was knock-your-socks-off.  The basil really stands out and it definitely warranted an audible moan.  The next few bites weren't as spectacular, but I still loved the sandwich.  I'd go with the Bird and Pig again if I had to choose.

While we waited, we treated our faces to black bean dip (suggested by the waiter) and we enjoyed it.  If you like black bean dip, then you'll like this one.  

We washed all of that down with a glass of liquid heroin, and all was right with the world.

The end.

Oh, and the service - spot on.  The place is cute, the staff is attentive, and it's clear this place easily doubles as a comfy daytime spot and a lovely night spot - if that's your kinda thing.

If you have ever dreamed of owning a bad ass bar and restaurant, with phenomenal and creative food, solid service, and atmosphere as cool as - well as cool as the bricks in the streets of Ybor City - don't go here. It will be likely to depress you to see that your dream has already been done so well that there just isnt much improvement. 
Well, if there was parking, that would be an improvement - but that's about it. I work nearby and rock their little patio in the back about once a week, it just never disappoints. The CURE is my favorite sandwich but i dont think there are any bad items on the menu - not even the vegetarian ones, and you know how bad those CAN be!

If you are on the west end of Ybor, or staying at the hotels nearby, or just stepped off the streetcar and want to figure out what Ybor City has come to mean these days - the Bricks of Ybor should be your first stop!

It isn't like the servers are slow either, they are clearly working their assess off running from table to table, so maybe it is that people have called in sick the couple of times I've been in recently and they had to work twice as hard but a Sunday lunch shouldn't take 3 hours. Now that my complaining is out of the way, the restaurant itself is super groovy. The kitchen is on full display so no crazy stories of chefs putting anything crazy into your food here. And they look like they are having a great time while they prepare meals (whether they are or not, I love to see people enjoy what they do). I normally get draft beer but their cocktails look really interesting and innovative. At lunch, I normally get the "Goodness" which is a hummus wrap and it comes with a choice of a side ($8). Don't bother being wishy-washy on the side, get the Asian slaw, it is delicous, and if available I would order as a meal. The wrap was good but the star was the slaw. Thai, pea-nutty, goodness:) I've gotten the Elvis before ($8) and it was deliciuos but something I can make a home. I ordered it without bacon. My husband ordered the burrito and loved it as well ($9). Others at our table raved about the Chicken and the Pig, The BBQ pork, and The Cure sandwiches. Everyone really liked their food. The Bricks really is a great spot on the 7th Avenue strip, perfect for late night people watching that make Ybor awesome and also out of the way enough to not feel like it's distinctly part of the Ybor scene.

Came for Father's day brunch, and will definitely come back. great selection of vegetarian food.  Veggie Cuban and cheese grits were awesome. .and service was so good!

2 words THE CURE! I ended up here after a night of one too many drinks (it happens). A friend recommended this place for a hang over cure! She was not mistaken! After reviewing their menu, which seemed a bit obnoxious, (I'm talking quirky names that require you read the description to be able to decipher what you're eating) I settled on the sandwich with an egg on it! Im a sucker for a runny egg on just about anything! Messy eggs, bacon, mozzarella, jalapeño aioli, on toasted cuban bread; this holy grail of a sandwich is called THE CURE! I have been back a few times to this establishment just for this sandwich, the mimosas too. Oh yea they have liquor so you can totally have drinks here. 

The ambience is very chill. There are a good amount of tables inside and bar seating; no outside seating. I have been here on a Sunday for brunch and found it to be pretty family/kid friendly. The whole place and most of the staff is painfully hipster but it works. The bathrooms are clean and there is a small back patio with mural art.
Bird and Pig and the Tuna BLT are awesome!  Delicious cold beer. Thanks for the recommendation, Yelp!
Great, laid-back atmosphere, terrific food. The ahi was good quality, as were the hummus and curry dip. We're going back for the peanut butter sandwiches.

The Bricks completely lives up to the hype. Don't leave without trying their amazing Basil-infused lemonade!

Really chill cafe-like vibe, with a creative comfort food menu (peanut butter sandwiches!), and full table service.

In a few weeks they will be opening a quiet "study hall" space for laptop lurkers, making this a killer telecommute/study spot.
Just went there yesterday for brunch...  I've had a ton of grilled cheese sandwiches but this makes my top five. Loved the atmosphere. So happy we gave this restaurant a chance.

I love the Bricks! We live in Ybor and this is one of our favorite lunch spots. I always have a hard time selecting between two sandwiches - The Elvis which is a peanut butter, banana and bacon sandwich or the Bird and Pig - roasted chicken, bacon, brie, apple, pressed on a Hawaiian sweet roll.

Bricks always offers weekly specials and featured drinks. The crowd is always fun and the staff is friendly.

My 2 favorite guy friends and I came here for Valentine's Day this year! I love everything about this place.  Every time I have visited there has been a friendly/diverse crowd and good music. I really like the atmosphere and the local artwork that is displayed throughout the restaurant. I highly recommend the brick layer nachos! My friends and I ate every bite and I honestly will most likely order that as my meal next time. The night we visited they had 50% off bottles of wine and after splitting the cost with one of my friends it was only $7 (need I say more?).  I ordered the brick layer salad with tuna for my meal. I ordered something lighter due to my massive nacho intake and the salad was good but it was similar to a house salad you can get anywhere. They have a very eclectic menu and next time I will probably try one of the many grilled cheese sandwiches listed on the menu. I will definitely be back!

Very fresh food- they actually make their own stuff! We ate lunch at the bar and the bartender went out of his way to help my husband find a good gluten free option. 

I ordered the black bean burger and it was delicious! Great atmosphere as well. Definitely recommend this place as there are not all that many fresh and relatively healthy places in the area. Wish we had found it sooner!

Came hungry and left full but not stuffed. The goodness wrap was named appropriately. Hummus with cucumber, tomato, lettuce, feta cheese and I added avocado was very flavorful. No need for any sauce of any kind. Had the potato salad as a side and though it was a bit bland, added a little salt to it, it was still good. Glad they don't add mayo to it and tasted home made for sure. Nice ambience too, decorated for Halloween. I'm not a fan of TV's while dining, but will always give a pass when they have good tunes playing so don't have to listen to TV. Only saw 2 servers on but it wasn't that busy on this Sunday afternoon. Server was knowledgeable and personable so not sure why others complained about rudeness. Saw none of that.
nice place for gatherings and hanging out. Friendly staff. Food was OK. Not bad, not good, it just sat somewhere in the middle.

How can you not like this place? Fresh water upon arrival followed by healthy food with a twist. The servise has always been exemplary so no complaints there. This is one of the few joints in Tampa that can appease an array of crowds - hipsters love the decor, drink selections, etc.; geriatrics enjoy the healthy food portions, friendliness, etc.; and out-of-towners relish the overall uniqueness of the place. This is beyond highly recommended.

Great location, cool atmosphere! The food was a fairly priced for the quality, which was good. I had the pulled pork tacos and they were not skimpy, fully stuffed and filling for $6. Great draft beer selection but it was a buck or two overpriced compared to other craft beer places. The two waitresses were very nice and pleasant. It was slow when we got there and them boom it was packed, they didn't forget about us but we did have to track her down for our last beer. I will be back for sure!

I have to say that the food here is good; however, the staff/service could be better. My sister and I came here for lunch and a few drinks. My sister ordered a drink off the menu and 10+min later, as we're finishing our lunch, the waitress comes back and says "sorry, our bartender doesn't know how to make that" ..... So the bartender doesn't know how to make the drinks listed on the menu? And the 10+mins. it took to tell us that, it could have ben googled and made. I don't want to bash this establishment, but the customer service has always been an issue here. I would reccomend continued training to both current and new staffers to improve their level of knowledge and customer srvice

The husband and I had a kid free day so we decided to have a (gasp) lunch date.

 We picked The Bricks because...well why the hell not.  As soon as we walked in I loved the place.  It was bright and cozy at the same time.  The staff was super friendly and we got the vibe that we could hang out all day if we wanted.

I ordered the most delicious "adult" coffee to drop kick the sleepiness out of my head.  The coffee was SUPER yummy and the liquor did the trick.

It took me a while to figure out what I wanted to eat because everything on the menu looked soooo good and I was super hungry.  In the end, I decided on the Harvest Grill Cheese Sandwich.....nom nom noom.....I was not dissappointed.  It hit the spot and filled my belly with melty cheesy goodness.  The bread was fresh, crunchy, tender and tasty.  The sandwich innards were porportioned perfect.  The Gouda, bacon and apple playing off each other in perfect harmony.

GO HERE AND EAT!  I cannot wait to go again and feel this will be a staple on our lunch resturant list.  Even if your not hungry this would be a wonderful place to have a drink and just chill day or night.

Thanks Bricks for a great lunch!
Great bar/café! Such a great place to hang, inside is beautiful and outside you can hear nice music while having a coffee and a cig! Definitely coming back! Loved it

I am not nearly cool enough to go here. The waiter was not unfriendly, but he was much more friendly to some ladies who sat near me with full sleeves of tattoos.  I ordered the black bean burger, it was so flavor less and thin it could have been omitted.  The mayo on the sandwich and mixed greens on the side,  along with the pickle,  we're the best part of the meal. My beer was alright,  but if I am going to spend $7 on a pint it should be delicious or high gravity,  this was neither, and since no prices appeared next to the draft list,  the price was a bit of a shock.

Since moving to Tampa about three weeks ago, I have found some ridiculously good restaurants thanks to Yelp and friends' recommendations. The Bricks has been on my list of places to try for a while now, and I finally made it last night. My friend & I walked in and were greeted immediately by the staff who told us to sit where we wanted. The place was fairly empty on a Tuesday at 7pm. I've heard it's packed on weekends, so perhaps going on off-nights is key. We started off with the Bricklayer, a fancy name for extra delicious nachos that are topped with queso, avocado cream, olives, and jalapeños. The salsa that comes on the side is awesome - super fresh, flavorful, and not too watery. This is a big appetizer and probably a bit too much for two girls before dinner. If I ordered it again, it would be as a bar snack rather than an app. For dinner, I had to try the Bird & the Pig. Wow - that pressed sweet bread combined with the salty bacon and chicken, paired with crisp apples and agave nectar? Yeah, the distinct flavors come together nicely to create one hell of a sandwich. I tasted my friend's black bean burger and liked that, too. The only thing I tasted that didn't blow me away was the roasted potato salad I got on the side. I'll probably just go with the mixed greens salad next time. Aside from the food, the environment is cool, too. I really liked all the local artists' work adorning the walls. There is ample parking nearby, including a garage on 15th that only charges $1 for the first 3 hours.

I loved this place, the food, atmosphere, and drinks and I was in Ybor one night and came in about midnight and walked back to use the restroom and then to sit down and get some food and drinks, typical of anyone that's out drinking and midnight rolls around. Well, I continue on the path to the restroom and the manager, yes, the manager, had the audacity to tell me if I proceeded to the restroom that he would come on after me. I thought he was joking. But no, he was serious, then he told me I needed to tip the bartender before using the restroom, even though I hadn't sat down to order anything yet. I was clearly upset and walked back out to leave. The guy at the door was very nice and lead me back in to use the restroom. I decided after being treated that way, by the manager, that this was not an establishment I would be frequenting any longer, even though I loved the place. I went to the restroom and came back out and put $3 on the bar, because I needed to "tip" to use the restroom. Well, the guy at the door said that the manager had ASSUMED that we came from a rave across the street and that we just wanted to use the restroom. Well, his assumption lost him business, and I have been living in the Bay Area for 32 years. I'm pretty sure telling a patron you are going to follow them into he women's restroom is some form of sexual harassment. I have NEVER been treated like that ever in an establishment. Hopefully, for the greater good of the restaurant, that manager is no longer there.

I thoroughly enjoy going to the Bricks.  It's unique atmosphere with cheap, but tasty, food options combine for a great experience.  

The term hipster is thrown around a lot these days and while you may be greeted and surrounded by people in skinny jeans, wearing Toms shoes, IMAX glasses, and an extra piercing, you are treated no differently.  I always feel warmly welcomed and entertained.  

As it does have a large bar, it may get rowdy in the evenings, but the Bricks maintains a family-friendly atmosphere.  

I ate the Bird and Pig meal once, very very good, and the breakfast bagel the next time.  The fiancee had black bean soup and a grilled cheese sandwich.  Very tasty combination. 

Highly recommend!

One of my favorite places to eat in Ybor! Good vibes, good food, and good drinks. Even their coffee is good! Service is a hit or miss, although most recently I have had consistent great service. And their veggie Cuban sandwich is amaaaazing!

While I was in Tampa for the last 2 years, The Bricks was a second home. Great food and even greater people. I moved back to Seattle and left making friends. Wish I could've brought The Bricks and my new friends back with me. Definitely a place for locals and visitors to check out!

I am not nearly cool enough to go here. The waiter was not unfriendly, but he was much more friendly to some ladies who sat near me with full sleeves of tattoos.  I ordered the black bean burger, it was so flavor less and thin it could have been omitted.  The mayo on the sandwich and mixed greens on the side,  along with the pickle,  we're the best part of the meal. My beer was alright,  but if I am going to spend $7 on a pint it should be delicious or high gravity,  this was neither, and since no prices appeared next to the draft list,  the price was a bit of a shock.

I'm definitely a fan.  The food/drinks are always stellar and while the staff is super friendly, the only issue with The Bricks is the time it takes to order/be served.  

It isn't like the servers are slow either, they are clearly working their assess off running from table to table, so maybe it is that people have called in sick the couple of times I've been in recently and they had to work twice as hard but a Sunday lunch shouldn't take 3 hours.  

Now that my complaining is out of the way, the restaurant itself is super groovy.  The kitchen is on full display so no crazy stories of chefs putting anything crazy into your food here.  And they look like they are having a great time while they prepare meals (whether they are or not, I love to see people enjoy what they do).  I normally get draft beer but their cocktails look really interesting and innovative.  

At lunch, I normally get the "Goodness" which is a hummus wrap and it comes with a choice of a side ($8).  Don't bother being wishy-washy on the side, get the Asian slaw, it is delicious, and if available I would order as a meal.  The wrap was good but the star was the slaw.  Thai, pea-nutty, goodness:)

I've gotten the Elvis before ($8) and it was delicious but something I can make a home.  I ordered it without bacon.  

My husband ordered the burrito and loved it as well ($9).  Others at our table raved about the Chicken and the Pig, The BBQ pork, and The Cure sandwiches.  Everyone really liked their food.  

The Bricks really is a great spot on the 7th Avenue strip, perfect for late night people watching that make Ybor awesome and also out of the way enough to not feel like it's distinctly part of the Ybor scene.
Just went there yesterday for brunch...  I've had a ton of grilled cheese sandwiches but this makes my top five. Loved the atmosphere. So happy we gave this restaurant a chance.

This was my first time here and I would recommend it! I had the Liquid Heroin (espresso, chocolate and milk) and the Bird and Pig. These two are the Bricks specialities. The Bird and Pig has chicken, bacon, apple, Brie, and honey. It is a perfect combination of salty and sweet. For dessert, we had the Ice Cream Sammy. A chocolate chip cookie with vanilla bean ice cream and chocolate syrup. I was a bit disappointed on the dessert because I was expecting the cookie to be soft and warm, it was the opposite; very hard. Overall the atmosphere is nice and I would come back to try some of the other specialties they have!

Yummy food, good vibes, & nice service. Music wasn't too loud. Could hold a conversation without hearing everyone else's. 

I had the Bird & Pig (the way it comes) with the Mac & Cheese. 

I also had the Hukilau. Not a fan. It sounded sweeter than it was. Still giving it a 4 for the food service and atmosphere. It's not their fault I didn't like the alcohol. 

Had a quick bite of the nachos and may have to orders those for the table next visit.
Great atmosphere and servise, food and drinks were exelent. Everything was fresh. Bird and the pig sandwich was delicious, also the pacific rim. Will return soon.

A couple of nights ago the Tampa Bay Lady Bloggers met at The Bricks for our monthly book club meeting. The staff was very welcoming and was happy to push together several tables for us. Our server was so nice and helpful and cheerfully took a group photo for us (annoying bloggers).

The "hole in the wall" atmosphere at The Bricks is fun and eclectic, with local art for sale lining the walls. I loved the laid-back, hip feeling of the place.

I had the "brick,paper,scissors" martini and it was so refreshing and delicious that I had to get a second with my entree. The table shared an order of the "bricklayer" nachos and they were okay, but the house-made salsa on the side was out of this world. For my entree I got the "bird and pig", based on so many great Yelp recommendations. It did not disappoint with thick, crispy bacon, sweet apples and agave nectar, tasty chicken and delicious pressed "sweet" bread. I almost caved in and got the Ahi tuna BLT because it looked so good on the menu...I'll definitely be back and try that next time to compare.

Thank you Bricks for hosting our meet-up. See you again soon I hope! My blog post about our meeting at The Bricks is here: http://carolinecalcote.com/2012/06/28/tampa-bay-lady-bloggers-book-club/
1st time we've tried The Bricks. So yummy!!! I had the Blackened Shrimp Salad and my husband had Sammy Tuna. We both loved every bite. Looking forward to eating there again.

Food was delish. Stopped before a concert at The Ritz, it is just a block away and the perfect stop for reasonably priced fresh, healthy-ish meal before you wreck your liver. BFF had the Bird and Pig, she loved it. I had the Blackstar Bean Burger. It was spicy which in my opinion was perfect. The drinks are pricy, but well crafted. Our service was meh. A little slow, but we received the correct order and were informed of specials and what they were out of before we decided. I will totally be back next time I am in town.
Easily my favorite overall spot in Ybor. The food is freaking amazing, the staff is awesome and know their booze/beer, and it just has a great feel.

This is THE BEST spot for food and drinks in Ybor.  The drinks are amazing and the food is top notch. Cool, laid back atmosphere and amazing bar!! All of the staff are helpful and accommodating!! Best happy hour!!!
Great, laid-back atmosphere, terrific food. The ahi was good quality, as were the hummus and curry dip. We're going back for the peanut butter sandwiches.

The Bricks is a tasty restaurant for lunch with a cool and unique Ybor City atmosphere along with friendly service! The only reason it didn't get 5 stars is because it is a little pricey for the quantities.
Bird and Pig and the Tuna BLT are awesome!  Delicious cold beer. Thanks for the recommendation, Yelp!

I had a good time at The Bricks of Ybor.  The service is really spot on and the quality of the food's pretty good.  I had the pulled pork sandwich.  It was pretty good.  Nothing memorable but what makes this place a four star place are the happy hour beer prices and the interesting art inside.

I loved the star wars art throughout this place and particularly loved the berpo and ern2d2 painting.

Friendly, fun crowd that looks like they're coming to a John Waters costume party.

I walk in, and they're playing the greatest hits of De La Soul throughout lunch. They could have been serving Big Macs and that gets you four stars alone. 

I order a grilled cheese sandwich, and it comes with apple, plums, and bacon on some delicious bread with tortilla chips. And it is sublime. The cheese is perfectly melted, and the goodies inside are covered in wonderful gooey dairy greatness. 

I order a cafe con leche while getting some work done on my laptop. It is flawlessly prepared by a lovely server, and I'm a coffee snob. And if I didn't get buried in work stuff, I was jonesing for one of those half-price martinis they serve on Thursdays.

Wonderful atmosphere (the skatepark staff makes it friendly and fun), great food, delicious coffee, a full bar, and lots of different options. This place is a total home run, and a can't miss for anyone in Ybor.

Lots of vegetarian options. The service was pretty fast. The skateboard wall was nice (Calvin & Hobbes represent!). The sandwich I got was a bit lacking in the flavor department. Really didn't know what to eat since I went here at night just before a binge of dancing and drinking. Didn't really feel into the peanut butter at that point in time. Next time I'll try their peanut butter creations, but I'll probably go for brunch or a late lunch since it seems the menu is more designed for that and not any pre-gaming.

We've heard that we need to go to places in Ybor and try them out, so we set out to find a place for dinner.  One thing is for sure...the menu has traditional food, but in a unique way.  

I ordered the deluxe grilled cheese (has tomatoes, pesto, whole wheat) and my husband had the BBQ pig quesadilla.  Both dishes were good, but I don't feel like they were 'awesome'.  

We went out on a limb and tried the hibiscus sangria and the chocolate espresso cake for dessert.  The cake was VERY espresso!  Too rich for me!  The sangria definitely tasted like flowers, but in a good way. It was pretty refreshing too!

 It was fun to try a new place, but I don't think we'll go back.

Highly recommend!
